OpenAI is testing a way to shield business prompts while its models run

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (306 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Thenextweb

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • OpenAI has started testing Private Inference, an alpha feature that uses confidential computing to protect business prompts and replies during processing, with a small group of customers.
  • It has been revealed that openAI has begun testing Private Inference with a small group of business customers.
  • According to recent reports, it uses confidential computing, which runs the work on sealed-off chips, plus “strict verifiable controls”, OpenAI’s product page says.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

OpenAI has started testing Private Inference, an alpha feature that uses confidential computing to protect business prompts and replies during processing, with a small group of customers. It joins Private Safety Processing in OpenAI’s Private Intelligence package, as Anthropic opens a rival safety system.

It has been revealed that openAI has begun testing Private Inference with a small group of business customers. The feature is meant to keep their prompts private while its models work on them. Chief executive Sam Altman unveiled the trial on X on Wednesday.

According to recent reports, it uses confidential computing, which runs the work on sealed-off chips, plus “strict verifiable controls”, OpenAI’s product page says. Apple takes a similar approach for Siri’s cloud requests.

OpenAI’s page calls Private Inference an alpha. The firm first indicated it at DevDay as a preview due this autumn.

“Stronger privacy protections will make frontier AI useful for a lot more work, and business privacy is important for a healthy ecosystem,” Altman wrote.

It has been revealed that private Inference is the second part of OpenAI’s privacy package for firms. The first, Private Safety Processing, checks for misuse without OpenAI keeping customer data. It began rolling out in September.

Recent findings suggest that shekar, who leads the work at OpenAI, called the test a first step. He said OpenAI is lining up more computing power for a much larger rollout, but gave no date.

It has been revealed that rival Anthropic has moved faster on safety checks. On Monday, it opened Enterprise Frontier Safeguards to all business owners in beta. The system watches for misuse while firms keep their own data.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, elevenLabs is in early talks for a funding round at a $33B valuation, planned for the first quarter of 2027, Bloomberg reported.
  • Industry observers note that elevenLabs is in early talks to raise money at a $33B valuation, Bloomberg reported on Wednesday, citing people familiar with the matter.
  • It has been revealed that that would be a 50% jump from the $22B ElevenLabs was valued at in a $300M share sale in September.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, elevenLabs is in early talks for a funding round at a $33B valuation, planned for the first quarter of 2027, Bloomberg reported. That would be 50% above its $22B valuation in September, and its annual recurring revenue has reached $700M, one person said.

Industry observers note that elevenLabs is in early talks to raise money at a $33B valuation, Bloomberg reported on Wednesday, citing people familiar with the matter. The voice AI company prepares to start the round in the first quarter of 2027, though some investors want it to begin sooner.

It has been revealed that that would be a 50% jump from the $22B ElevenLabs was valued at in a $300M share sale in September. It also fits the company’s habit of setting valuations in multiples of 11, a nod to its name.

According to recent reports, elevenLabs’ annual recurring revenue has reached $700M, one person told Bloomberg, up from the $600M it reported in September. ElevenLabs declined to comment.

Sources indicate that the price would be steep next to its peers. London video AI firm Synthesia was valued at $4B in January with about $140M in yearly revenue. Mistral was valued at €21B in September, having passed $400M early in the year.

Investors may be spurred on by Anthropic’s record $107.3B IPO, which brought early backers huge gains.

ElevenLabs was founded in London in 2022 by Mati Staniszewski and Piotr Dabkowski, and makes realistic AI voices for games, audiobooks and AI agents. Staniszewski has mentioned it could start preparing for an IPO in 2028.

Back in 2024, developer Simon Støvring rolled out Festivitas, an app that brings a ton of holiday cheer to your Mac. This year, the app is getting even more whimsical and delightful with new snowfall features.

For those unfamiliar, Festivitas lets you hang lights of different colors and patterns from your Mac’s menu bar and dock. It has a bunch of different customization options, so you can tweak the lights to match your preferences.

Last year, the app added a fresh snowfall effect alongside those Christmas lights, plus Shortcuts integration and a dedicated iPhone and iPad app with customizable widgets.

This year’s Festivitas enhancement expands that snowfall feature. Now, the snow that falls from the top of your Mac’s screen can pile up at the bottom of your screen, and you can use your mouse to shovel it away. This joins the existing ability to adjust snow amount, flake size, fall speed, and wind direction.

Head to the Festivitas website to get started and bring some holiday cheer to your Apple devices.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Perplexity’s artwork for its Time Machine API.

According to recent reports, perplexity has added Time Machine to its Search and Context APIs, letting agents see the web as it was up to 365 days ago so forecasting tests are not spoiled by hindsight. It follows Epochal’s Time Portal by a day, and Perplexity’s results come from its own tests.

Perplexity has released Time Machine, a tool that lets AI agents search the web as it looked on a past date, the company remarked on Wednesday. It arrived a day after Epochal, a startup from three of xAI’s co-founders, launched a similar product.

Both target the same problem. An AI agent asked about a past election or earnings call can simply look up the result. That makes it hard to test how well it really predicts.

Time Machine adds a date cutoff to Perplexity’s search and page-reading tools for developers, so results come from copies saved before that date. Perplexity’s cutoffs reach back 365 days. Epochal states its archive spans more than 30 years.

According to recent reports, perplexity claims it used the tool to train an AI model to forecast 2026 political events listed on Polymarket. In its own test, the trained model scored 0.80, just above the market’s 0.79.

According to recent reports, it also indicates fewer of its pages leaked later information than rival Exa’s, at 0.25% against 1.10% in one test. That was judged by Perplexity’s own automated checker. Time Machine costs the same as Perplexity’s other API calls.

It has been revealed that web tools built for AI agents are multiplying. On the same day, Cloudflare began letting websites offer agents their own search.

Archives of the web are becoming contested ground. More than 241 news outlets now block the Wayback Machine to keep AI companies away from their old articles.

[ about | demo | using it | how it works | code | warning! | links ].

minipg is PostgreSQL as one executable, ready to use, with no server to configure. A .pgdb directory is the database: its data, config, credentials, and Postgres version all live inside it, and minipg app.pgdb opens a psql shell on it. A server starts when a command needs one and stops on its own when it's idle.

minipg embeds Docker Hub's postgres:18-alpine image and runs it with h9, used as a Zig library. h9's Linux personality runs Alpine's own Postgres binaries directly on the host's hypervisor, with h9's Strategy 9 kernel answering their system calls. There's no Linux kernel to boot, no VM image, and no Docker.

The demo downloads about 35 MB. It needs JavaScript Promise Integration, which Chrome and Edge have from version 137; other browsers are getting it. It can also be opened on its own page.

The demo runs minipg's Linux build, which runs inside the Postgres image itself. It starts Postgres as ordinary processes and serves on a unix socket, since a page has no TCP. Fresh databases come from a template cluster made at build time, because initdb takes half a minute on v86.

A .pgdb holds minipg.toml (settings and the generated superuser password) and pgdata/, Postgres's data directory as plain files. A stopped one can be copied like any directory. Fresh clusters use Postgres's builtin C.UTF-8 locale, which sorts the same on every platform.

In CI, the Linux binary is static and needs no privileges or devices: without /dev/kvm, h9 runs Postgres on its native backend. A test job can be as small as:.

The README lists every command, and the manual is the full guide.

Recent findings suggest that exactly one process runs Postgres for a .pgdb, enforced by a lock. It holds the server's h9 machine, whose Linux root is the unpacked image and whose writable working directory is the .pgdb. The image's docker-entrypoint.sh initializes the cluster on first start. Commands never host Postgres themselves. If no server is running, they start one in the background and use it. psql, pg_dump, and the other tools each run in their own short-lived h9 machine (about 90 ms to start) over the same root.

Industry observers note that the source is on GitHub, under the MIT license. Building needs Zig 0.16, plus curl, jq, tar, and xz for the root:.

minipg is early, and h9's Linux personality is young. On h9's native backend, Postgres is about 2x slower than native for one client, and slower under load. Don't trust it with data you can't recreate yet.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Elon Musk speaks with press outside the West Wing after a White House luncheon on superintelligence on 29 September 2026.

Elon Musk has pledged to give every child in the US two shares of SpaceX, doubling a promise he made last month, and at the current prices, the gift is worth about $18bn.

Every child in America will receive two SpaceX shares, one from the tech giant and one from me personally.

— Elon Musk (@elonmusk) November 26, 2026.

According to recent reports, spaceX stated in a statement the same day that it would contribute one newly issued share of its Class A common stock to every currently active Trump Account. Elon Musk will then match the manufacturer’s gift with one share of his own for each account.

Trump Accounts are government-backed investment accounts for children under 18, created under the 2025 tax and spending law and opened for contributions in July.

The White House remarked in October that almost 70 million accounts had been opened.

Because the shares go only to active accounts, a child needs a Trump Account to receive them. Any child under 18 with a valid Social Security number can have one, although only those born between 2025 and 2028 also get the government’s $1,000 deposit.

There are about 72 million children in the US, according to Census Bureau estimates, and with SpaceX shares closing at $127.44 on Wednesday, two shares each would come to roughly $18bn, making it the largest private pledge to the programme so far.

Before this, the biggest gift came from Michael and Susan Dell, who pledged more than $6bn in December 2025 to add $250 to millions of children’s accounts.

SpaceX president Gwynne Shotwell has also pledged her own shares, one each for roughly 2 million children.

Industry observers note that musk first raised the idea on 19 October, promising every child one SpaceX share next year and calling it the first of many. Yet Wednesday’s announcement did not give a latest date for when the shares will reach the accounts.

The gift is a small slice of Musk’s fortune, as about $650bn of his roughly $820bn net worth is held in SpaceX stock, according to the Bloomberg Billionaires Index.

He also keeps majority voting control of the tech giant through its two classes of shares.

SpaceX has been public since its Nasdaq listing in June, and the money held in a Trump Account generally cannot be withdrawn until the child turns 18.

  • The New York Times is asking freelance photographers not to use the newest version of Adobe Photoshop because features in the 2027 update use AI “in ways that may not be apparent to users.” In an email seen by The Verge and posted on Threads, two of the Times’ photography leaders, Meaghan Looram and Josh Haner, write that the use of these features “can result in metadata identifying photographs as AI-generated.”.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

An email sent to freelance photographers indicates Photoshop’s latest patch uses AI ‘in ways that may not be apparent.’.

An email sent to freelance photographers states Photoshop’s latest revision uses AI ‘in ways that may not be apparent.’.

The New York Times is asking freelance photographers not to use the newest version of Adobe Photoshop because features in the 2027 update use AI “in ways that may not be apparent to users.” In an email seen by The Verge and posted on Threads, two of the Times’ photography leaders, Meaghan Looram and Josh Haner, write that the use of these features “can result in metadata identifying photographs as AI-generated.”.

Adobe has spent the past few years filling Photoshop and other apps in its creative suite with a trove of AI-powered tools. The November update cited by the NYT’s email adds several latest AI features, including Adobe’s new “AI Assisted Editor” view, which lets owners access all of Photoshop’s AI features from a single toolbar. It also adds an AI assistant for step-by-step editing instructions, prompt-based image transformation and editing, new AI upscaling options, and an AI-powered tool that recomposes images for different canvas sizes.

It has been revealed that it’s not always clear which tools in Adobe’s apps are AI-powered, and even some older options like automated selection tools may now be considered part of the AI suite. This can lead to photos ending up with metadata indicating they were edited with AI, which is a blunt way of describing what happened in post-production. For a newsroom like the Times, where photo editing is kept to a minimum, the metadata risks losing readers’ trust. Last year, the Times mentioned that it does not “retouch or digitally manipulate” photos but may “make minimal adjustments to color to ensure we are accurately reproducing the image.”.

It has been revealed that in August, Adobe began rolling out support for C2PA metadata across its apps, which indicates whether an image is AI-generated or edited using AI features. The NYT is issuing its restriction to keep these tags from inadvertently appearing in its photos. “At this time, we are requiring that all contributing photographers avoid using Adobe Photoshop 2027 (release 28.0.0 and subsequent updates) when working on assignment for The Times,” the email reads. NYT spokesperson Graham James confirmed the requirement in a statement to The Verge, which reiterated the policy outlined in the email.

Sources indicate that it’s still not clear which specific Photoshop features the NYT is referring to. Adobe didn’t immediately respond to The Verge’s request for more information.

Patch, November 24th: Added confirmation from the NYT.

According to recent reports, whatsApp just declared that it is rolling out scheduled messages, which it notes is one of users’ most requested features. Here are the details.

From WhatsApp’s blog post announcing support for scheduled messages:.

You can write a message when you think of it and send it anywhere from 10 minutes to 14 days later, in both your 1:1 and group chats.

To schedule a message, press and hold the send button and pick the date and time you want it to arrive. It will look like any other message to the person receiving it. You can see all future messages you have lined up, and delete them beforehand if you change your mind.

Even if your phone is off or out of battery, your scheduled message will still show up at the time you chose, and it remains end-to-end encrypted like all your personal messages, so no one else can read it, not even us.

WhatsApp says this feature is “rolling out globally over the coming weeks.” So you might not see it right away, but even if you don’t, it should show up on your account soon.

Scheduled messages work not only for text, but also when sending media like photos and videos.

To get access to scheduled messages, make sure you’ve updated to the latest WhatsApp app patch, which was just released today.

In other WhatsApp news, earlier today we reported that stickers with audio are coming soon, including user-created options.

It has been revealed that britBox is a streaming paradise packed with British television from the BBC and ITV. Industry observers note that you likely have a spare lying around already, probably the one you made in 2011 and now use exclusively for receipts. If not, any of the many email services with a free tier will do the trick, whether that's Gmail, Yahoo, Outlook or AOL.

Here's my annual routine. Last year, Past Me, a surprisingly responsible person, set calendar reminders to cancel everything I signed up for during Black Friday week. Then I take my fresh email address and go deal hunting. The ones I think are worth your money every year are Peacock, HBO Max and Paramount+.

In a recent development, in a word: no. Netflix doesn't do Black Friday. I check every year, and every year I'm met with the same cold, red-logoed silence.

Munich fusion startup Starforge raises €6.6M to build reactors in factories

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Starforge co-founders Dr Ana Koller (left), CEO, and Jonathan Janssen, COO.
  • Munich startup Starforge has raised €6.6M to build fusion reactors on production lines, instead of one power plant at a time, with AENU and First Momentum Ventures leading the pre-seed round.
  • Auxxo, Kvanted, Silicon Roundabout Ventures, UnternehmerTUM Funding for Innovators, and Arcas also joined the round, which the firm closed in eight weeks over the summer.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Starforge co-founders Dr Ana Koller (left), CEO, and Jonathan Janssen, COO.

Munich startup Starforge has raised €6.6M to build fusion reactors on production lines, instead of one power plant at a time, with AENU and First Momentum Ventures leading the pre-seed round.

Auxxo, Kvanted, Silicon Roundabout Ventures, UnternehmerTUM Funding for Innovators, and Arcas also joined the round, which the firm closed in eight weeks over the summer.

The deal arrives in a busy year for the sector, with 17 fusion startups now having raised more than $100M each.

Dr Ana Koller and Jonathan Janssen founded the organization in March. Koller previously worked at Commonwealth Fusion Systems, MIT, and the Max Planck Institute for Plasma Physics, while Janssen is a former executive at flying-taxi maker Lilium and at GE.

Rather than generate and sell electricity itself, the manufacturer looks to sell its reactors to utilities, governments, and private owners.

That mirrors how Westinghouse and Framatome supply reactors for fission plants today, leaving turbines and grid connections to others.

Each reactor would produce 200 to 300 megawatts of electricity, within the size range the International Atomic Energy Agency uses for small modular reactors.

Starforge has chosen the spherical tokamak, a compact version of the doughnut-shaped machines that use magnets to hold superheated plasma in place.

Recent findings suggest that because buyers could add capacity one unit at a time, the company sees customers beyond national grids, from data centres to industrial heating and remote defence sites. Its first reactor, Unit One, will use superconducting magnets that can be taken apart.

That way, parts can be serviced in the field over a working life of more than 40 years.

“Starforge wants to make fusion boring: a utility people drive past without a second thought,” mentioned Koller, the firm’s chief executive.

It has been revealed that the factory model is meant to bring prices down as volumes grow. Starforge expects each doubling of production to cut costs by 15%, and is aiming for electricity at around 5 cents per kilowatt-hour once its reactors are built in fleets.

Industry observers note that recent research has been more cautious about how swiftly fusion can get cheaper. An ETH Zurich study published in Nature Energy in April put the likely cost decline at 2% to 8% for each doubling of capacity, against 23% for solar modules. Starforge’s bet is that factory production can beat that curve.

It has been revealed that the company is building in a country whose government wants to host the world’s first fusion power plant, and which launched a €500M programme for fusion startups in October. Munich is already home to Proxima Fusion, which raised a record €411M round.

Over the next 24 months, Starforge will use the capital to grow its team, finish the conceptual design of Unit One, and secure its first customer commitments in Europe. Moreover, the company is targeting commercial operations in the mid-2030s.

Black Friday shopping can be exhausting, especially when you're juggling multiple wish lists, comparing prices and trying to stick to a budget. But this year, Walmart is giving shoppers the option to hand some of that work over to AI.

On Tuesday, Walmart declared a partnership with Meta that lets customers shop its Black Friday deals through Muse, Meta's personal AI agent.

Unlike traditional AI chatbots that recommend products and send you links, Muse can take you through the purchasing process without leaving the conversation. Of course, you'll still have to actually approve the purchase, but it could be helpful when time is of the essence.

And if you're nervous about giving AI access to your credit card, Walmart has built in some safeguards.

Let's say you're looking for a blender but you don't want to spend your entire afternoon comparing models. You can tell Muse what you're looking for, how much you're willing to spend and whether you need it delivered.

Walmart handles the product matching behind the scenes through its fresh Agent Gateway.

According to the retailer, shoppers will have access to the same prices available on Walmart.com, including Black Friday discounts and applicable membership benefits.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

Walmart also claims the integration doesn't expose your broader shopping history to third-party agents.

I decided to give this a try (hopefully my husband isn't reading this). I started by simply heading to Muse.ai. From there, I described what I wanted. You can be as descriptive as you want or even vague. I simply gave the prompt, "My husband does a lot of yard work and I'd like to find a gift to help make the job easier." I didn't give a budget (it prompted me "what's your budget?) or any other specific requirements, but you can up front to make shopping even more personal and streamlined. Once you've done that, you're going to want to do the following:.

Connect your Walmart account. Muse will direct you to Walmart to sign in before returning you to the conversation.

Industry observers note that set your spending limit. When adding your first product, you'll create a Walmart Agent Profile to manage what the AI is authorized to do.

Recent findings suggest that complete your purchase. You can check out directly through the conversation with your existing Walmart payment method.Muse showed me a few items before completing the purchase. Rest assured it does pause so you can see the choices. My husband has many of the items on the list already, so that hesitation was appreciated. Since my credit card is already connected to Walmart, this safeguard is key. The last thing I want is to spend hundreds of dollars on yard equipment we already have!

Walmart's regular return policy still applies to purchases made through Muse.

The more specific you are about what you need, the more useful AI shopping could be. If you're looking for someone on your list who is difficult to shop for like a teenage boy, this Muse partnership could be a lifesaver. Here are five prompts worth trying.

"Find me the best Black Friday deal on a 55-inch 4K TV under $300 at Walmart.".

"Help me buy Christmas gifts for three kids ages 6, 9 and 12 with a total budget of $150.".

"Find five tech gifts under $25 that are at the moment discounted at Walmart.".

"Find the best Black Friday deals on wireless headphones under $100. Prioritize battery life and noise cancellation.".

"Help me find stocking stuffers for four people without spending more than $50 total.".

I'd recommend including instructions to show you the individual prices and total cost before completing any purchase.

Between shopping lists, crowded stores and seemingly endless Black Friday sales, there's certainly an appeal to having AI take care of some of the legwork.

It has been revealed that but I'd still recommend double-checking product specifications, customer reviews and prices at competing retailers before letting an AI agent make a purchase. Just because something is discounted doesn't necessarily mean it's the best deal.

Walmart states it prepares to bring its shopping experience to additional AI agents and apps in the future. For now, Muse offers another way to tackle your holiday shopping list without opening dozens of browser tabs.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, according to a new Counterpoint Research report, Apple increased its share of Latin America’s smartphone shipments in Q3 2026, recording the smallest decline among the region’s top five brands. Here are the details.

In a report released this week, Counterpoint Research states the ongoing memory crunch led to a 24% year-over-year drop in smartphone shipments during Q3, “the second-lowest quarter since 2015.”.

Recent findings suggest that per the report, Samsung maintained its lead with a 35% shipment share, despite a 15% year-over-year decline in total shipments, well ahead of second-place Motorola, which captured 18% of shipments after a 23% drop. Interestingly, Motorola’s share actually increased one percentage point from a year earlier.

Rounding out the top five were Xiaomi, with a 14% share and a whopping 34% decline, Apple, with a 9% share and a 10% decline, and Honor, with an 8% share and a 27% decline.

Despite the decline in overall shipments, Apple’s shipment share increased by 2 percentage points from 7% a year earlier, moving the company from fifth to fourth place in the region.

Other brands collectively accounted for 16% of shipments, down from 19% a year earlier, with their combined shipments falling 37% year over year.

Here’s Counterpoint on Apple’s performance for Q3 in Latin America:.

According to recent reports, apple was the most resilient, with the smallest decline among the top five brands (shipments down 10% YoY), and rose one position to No. 4 in the region. Apple absorbed the impact of price increases better than its rivals, helped by strong product availability. Apple released the iPhone 18 Pro series at the end of the quarter. For the first time, Chile joined Brazil and Mexico in the first launch wave.

As for regional factors that contributed to the decline, Senior Analyst Benjamin Corona noted that Brazil, Mexico, and Colombia faced additional challenges beyond the global memory shortage, ranging from political uncertainty to inflation and tighter household budgets. Smartphone shipments fell 22%, 26%, and 28% in those countries, respectively.

Looking ahead, Counterpoint says it “expects the decline to ease in Q4 2026 as prices stabilize and seasonal demand returns,” adding that “memory-related price pressure should moderate by Q2 2027, but supply constraints will likely continue through the end of 2027.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

John Lions was teaching operating systems at the University of Upcoming South Wales in Australia.

What's the best way toteach operating systems?

They need to study the Unix source.But it's tough going.

Sources indicate that in May 1976, Lions prepared lecture notes explaining the kernel source code of AT&T's Unix Version 6. These became his Unix commentary.

To understand an OS,we need to readthe actual code.

I've written a guideto the Unix kernel.We'll use it asour textbook.

In a recent development, by 1977, the notes were circulating among other schools and research institutions with Unix licenses [1][4]. Even Bell Labs wanted copies and eventually took over distribution [2].

Early on, Unix source could be studied in class. But at USENIX in June 1979, AT&T announced newly introduced Version 7 license terms restricting courses that disclosed or discussed source code. Distribution of Lions' book was tightly controlled as well [5][6].

I am altering the license.Pray I don't alter itany further.

Destroy Lions' book.No more teachingUnix source code.

There is no escapefrom our operating system.

He's teaching from the Unix source code!Seize the books!Run!

I find your interestin source code disturbing.

Just use the system calls.Learn a little theory.Leave the internals to us.

Theory isn't enough.I need to see the code.

This code is our only hopeof understanding an OS.

For roughly twenty years before the official edition appeared, computer-science students studied from unauthorized photocopies. The book helped a generation of students learn to build operating systems of their own [5][8].

Industry observers note that meanwhile, members of the Unix community, including Peter H. Salus, Dennis Ritchie and Berny Goodheart, kept asking AT&T, Novell and the Santa Cruz Operation for permission to publish the book. SCO finally agreed. Peer-to-Peer Communications published the official edition in 1996 [5][7].

Lions' book is finallyin print. It even hasmy foreword.

People were secretly copying itfor twenty years?Unbelievable.

You can read a reconstructed version of the commentary as a PDF, or order a print copy on Amazon. The Unix Version 6 source code is available separately from TUHS.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AI-powered workspaces are tech companies’ latest focus, as the industry still struggles to perfect adoption. Microsoft has just put its offering into the ring.

During the keynote for the tech giant’s Ignite conference on Tuesday, CEO Satya Nadella revealed Copilot Workspaces, a collaborative, “multiplayer” surface for Copilot’s agentic capabilities.

Also: Microsoft says its new AI coding model rivals Claude Opus 5.5 at 5% of the cost.

The product, available in Frontier for now, is similar to OpenAI’s ChatGPT Space and several fresh Anthropic features, including Whiteboard and Sheets, which essentially merge the work tools you’re used to using with an agentic framework.

Recent findings suggest that “As the evolution of Copilot Notebooks, it’s where people and agents build on each other’s work,” Microsoft remarked. “An agent drafts a section of a document, and you review. You leave a comment, and an agent picks it up.”.

Microsoft also announced Autopilot, a sort of counterpoint agent to Copilot that “can watch Teams channels, follow up on emails, run recurring work, and manage a project — without waiting for a prompt,” as Microsoft described.

In a demo video during the keynote, the agent appeared to function similarly to OpenAI’s Dots, but for work — employees can tag their Autopilot “like a colleague,” Microsoft said, and assign it tasks.

Also: 4 ways Anthropic’s latest Claude Sheets beat using a Google Sheets connector.

Microsoft stated the agent will be able to autonomously handle “meetings and follow-ups on its own,” though that claim may be best verified by teams themselves.

Speaking of trust, however, Microsoft noted that “Autopilot runs on the identity, security, and compliance foundation IT already uses,” and that “each Autopilot has its own Microsoft Entra Agent ID and a named manager,” meaning IT can block it as needed.

“Its sign-ins and actions are logged under its own name, so security teams have a clear audit trail. Powered by Work IQ, it understands how your organization works within existing permissions,” Microsoft stated.

Sources indicate that the company added that employees will soon “be able to bring their personal Autopilot into Workspaces” as well. The feature is also available in Frontier.

Sources indicate that nadella also declared a few other productivity features, including a “command center” called Today that spans email, calendar, meetings, tasks, and threads in Teams. Currently in private preview in Outlook and the Copilot app, it includes a personalized briefing and a feed of priorities that updates throughout the day.

“The draft is written and ready for you to edit; the schedule change is already proposed; and the forgotten follow-up is waiting for you to send it, complete with context so you can catch up rapidly,” Microsoft remarked of the feature, which sounds like an agentic briefing-cum-morning-assistant.

Also: Nearly 70% of workers use AI regularly now – but many get no time to upskill.

Microsoft also declared that Home, now generally available, unifies Chat and Cowork into a singular starting point. That’s similar to Anthropic’s recent consolidation of its chat and agentic Cowork offerings, demonstrating an overall trend toward simplification in workplace AI.

While more companies are finally starting to see a return on their AI investment, agents are still expensive and can swiftly rack up costs when unsupervised.

Microsoft revealed a few tools to track this at Ignite: Agent 365 Business Analytics and Agent 365 Cost Management.

Also: Microsoft wants to put a dollar value on AI’s work – but can you trust the math?

Industry observers note that agent 365, which Microsoft declared last year, is the firm’s observability platform. Microsoft said Business Analytics, in Frontier Public today, provides insights on what a company is spending on AI and why, and where it’s paying off, as well as forecasts future costs. In a demo during the keynote, Microsoft showed how admins can see when specific agents’ costs have spiked recently and what (human) employee to notify as a result.

“It starts with a newly introduced way to measure your investment: in work completed, not simply tokens,” Microsoft noted. “It analyzes the tasks, how long that work typically takes a person, and the share Cowork performed, providing a sophisticated view of the hours your intelligence supports and what the work is worth.”.

Cost Management lets IT see where teams are using AI down to the model.

It has been revealed that “Leaders can set spending policies, limits, and proactive alerts and control which models are available,” Microsoft said. Anthropic released a similar tool last month, though it was focused more on making seats as efficient as possible on Teams and Enterprise aims.

Screens 5.10 delivered two highly-requested desktop features to consumers earlier this month. Now the app is back with a fun enhancement for iPhone Duo users: tiny laptop mode.

It has been revealed that iPhone Duo supports various positions including a partially opened configuration. iOS 27 allows apps to respond to the hinge position, offering unique experiences as a result.

Edovia, the makers of Screens, took this as an opportunity to make the remote desktop viewer transform iPhone Duo into what it looks like in this mode: a very miniature notebook computer.

“Simply fold your iPhone Duo halfway to turn it into a pocket-sized workstation, with your remote desktop on the upper half and a custom keyboard and trackpad below,” Edovia says.

“The trackpad supports the same familiar gestures you’ve come to expect from Screens, while the custom keyboard supports multiple languages, follows your selected system keyboard language, and lets you swipe down on keys to access secondary characters, just like on iPad.”.

They show off the revision in full on their website here. Screens for iPhone Duo is available on the App Store.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, during the keynote at its Ignite conference on Tuesday, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella announced several new models from Microsoft AI (MAI), its lab within the company.
  • Also: Microsoft states its fresh AI coding model rivals Claude Opus 5.5.
  • Industry observers note that MAI said it would allow its customers to customize its frontier models with their own data and run them securely in Azure through an initiative called Licensed Weights.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, during the keynote at its Ignite conference on Tuesday, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella announced several new models from Microsoft AI (MAI), its lab within the company. But new model releases are almost a dime a dozen these days, and accelerating fast — what really stood out was how Microsoft will let its customers access those models.

Also: Microsoft states its fresh AI coding model rivals Claude Opus 5.5.

Industry observers note that MAI said it would allow its customers to customize its frontier models with their own data and run them securely in Azure through an initiative called Licensed Weights. It’s essentially a selective approach to open-weight AI: more so than proprietary models from OpenAI and Anthropic, but not fully downloadable on Hugging Face like Mistral’s Le Chonk. Interested companies will need to go through their Microsoft account reps to get started.

“You control who can access it. Your data and adaptations stay entirely yours. And we’ll work with you through Frontier Organization to deliver the custom model and embed it in your own products and agents,” Mustafa Suleyman, CEO of MAI, stated during the keynote.

The approach should stand out to businesses looking for affordable AI that lets them retain control over their IP. Microsoft mentioned it would only use customers’ information to train its models if they agreed.

“No one wants to pour their IQ into someone else’s model,” Suleyman mentioned during the keynote, a nod to an argument Palantir CEO Alex Karp has made repeatedly.

Sources indicate that the dominant, if simplified, narrative in AI has been that proprietary, expensive models boast peak capabilities but aren’t customizable, while open, cheaper models are customizable but less capable. Microsoft’s AI models don’t necessarily compete with OpenAI and Anthropic yet, but the manufacturer has legacy sway with countless businesses. By offering a customizable AI option, it could strike a balance among major tech companies.

Recent findings suggest that western labs, including Thinking Machines and Mistral, are releasing more competitive open-weight models, but Anthropic and OpenAI still have the overwhelming majority of the enterprise AI market. Though Licensed Weights isn’t an open-weight family of models, it does diversify the open-versus-closed debate a bit and differentiate Microsoft’s offering from OpenAI’s and Anthropic’s. It’s also a smart pairing with Microsoft’s goal to balance price and performance, if businesses find it impressive enough.

Also: Microsoft unveiled Copilot Workspaces at Ignite 2026.

“Averaged over four widely used benchmarks that target the everyday enterprise coding tasks we see in GitHub Copilot, MAI Code 2 gives you 98% of the performance of GPT 6.1 Sol at just 40% of the cost, and against Opus 5.5 it’s an incredible 5% of that cost,” Suleyman said of the new coding model the company confirmed at Ignite.

The company also released its new image editing model, MAI Image 2.7, on Tuesday, which now leads the category on Artificial Analysis while beating Nano Banana Pro and several GPT image models on price and quality. With Licensed Weights, Microsoft has positioned itself for organizations seeking a reliable blend of ROI tools, customization, security controls, and capability.

Major developers, legal experts, and 32 states back Epic in Apple’s SCOTUS appeal

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that in a significant development in Apple’s Supreme Court appeal of a civil contempt ruling, Epic Games has received backing from 32 states and the District of Columbia, along with major developers, legal experts, former federal judges, and more.
  • Apple’s ever-sprawling fight against Epic Games over its App Store policies is currently being fought on two fronts: in the Supreme Court, where Apple is seeking to overturn a civil contempt ruling, and in the district court, where the companies are disputing what commission, if any, Apple can charge on purchases made through external payment systems.
  • The civil contempt ruling came after Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers found that Apple had violated an earlier injunction issued in its App Store dispute with Epic.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that in a significant development in Apple’s Supreme Court appeal of a civil contempt ruling, Epic Games has received backing from 32 states and the District of Columbia, along with major developers, legal experts, former federal judges, and more. Here are the details.

Apple’s ever-sprawling fight against Epic Games over its App Store policies is currently being fought on two fronts: in the Supreme Court, where Apple is seeking to overturn a civil contempt ruling, and in the district court, where the companies are disputing what commission, if any, Apple can charge on purchases made through external payment systems.

The civil contempt ruling came after Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers found that Apple had violated an earlier injunction issued in its App Store dispute with Epic.

In a nutshell, after she ordered Apple to allow developers to direct people to alternative payment methods outside the App Store, the tech giant responded by allowing external payment links, but imposed a commission of up to 27% on purchases made through them.

Since then, Apple has been trying to overturn the civil contempt ruling, basically arguing that the original injunction did not explicitly prohibit the commissions and other restrictions it imposed on external purchases.

After the Ninth Circuit upheld the contempt finding and denied its request for rehearing, Apple took the case to the Supreme Court, which agreed to hear its appeal.

Importantly, the Supreme Court will only consider the legal standard used to uphold Apple’s civil contempt ruling, not the separate question of what commission, if any, the company can charge on purchases made through external payment methods.

That will still be determined in the district court, where proceedings have continued despite Apple’s attempts to put them on hold pending the Supreme Court’s decision.

With oral arguments scheduled for January 11, 2027, the case has recently seen a flurry of activity, including Apple’s opening brief in September and Epic’s response earlier this month.

Apple also received support from several organizations in September, including the Washington Legal Foundation, the International Center for Law and Economics, the Computer & Communications Industry Association, and the U.S. Chamber of Commerce. The US government also submitted a brief supporting neither party, arguing that the contempt finding was unjustified over Apple’s 27% commission, but warranted over its restrictions on button designs.

Which brings us to the latest developments: a series of amicus briefs filed in support of Epic Games.

Last week, a total of 9 amicus briefs were filed in support of Epic Games, including one led by Utah and joined by 31 other states and the District of Columbia.

This particular brief notes that “the district court correctly held Apple in contempt for continuing to engage in anticompetitive conduct barred by a prior injunction,” adding:.

“The court found that Apple engaged in unlawful anti-steering restrictions and required Apple to lift those restrictions. Apple then lifted them in name only, imposed fresh (and substantially similar) strictures on developers that mirrored the old ones and produced the same result. Worse still, Apple did all this in bad faith: Apple knew its behavior was wrong and actively hid that fact from the court, including by providing false testimony. Under any reasonable reading of the district court’s injunction, Apple’s conduct is worthy of civil contempt.”.

The states also argue that “Injunctions in competition cases cannot afford complete relief without addressing the ongoing effects of anticompetitive behavior,” and that “[c]onstruing competition injunctions narrowly defeats their purpose and prevents meaningful redress.”.

Similar arguments appear throughout the other briefs, which include submissions from Spotify, Match Group, and Microsoft, as well as nonprofit organizations such as the American Antitrust Institute (AAI), Public Knowledge, and the Electronic Frontier Foundation (EFF).

In their joint brief, Spotify, Match Group, and Microsoft argue that they “have first-hand experience with the effects of Apple’s conduct and evasion efforts,” adding that “Apple’s fresh restrictions were no different from the unlawful rules they replaced.”.

As for the brief filed by former federal judges, they warned that “[i]n cases like these, where enjoined parties seek to circumvent an injunction through reliance on its literal text, courts must have the power of contempt to deter and remedy evasion. Otherwise, courts would be forced into a game of whack-a-mole, trying to anticipate every possible means of evading an injunction […]”.

Arguments by the Little Tech Association, AAI, Public Knowledge, and the EFF all follow a similar line, with some also addressing how Apple’s restrictions on external payment links could affect consumer choice, pricing, and competition.

Here’s the full list of parties that filed amicus briefs in support of Epic Games:.

Industry observers note that ubuntu 27.04, Tenacious T-Rex, is set for an April 22, 2027 release. Although that seems a long way off, it’s sooner than you think. As is implied by the release number, 27.04 is not an LTS release, so it only receives support for nine months (until January 2028). The good news is that you can migrate from 27.04 to 27.10, and then to the LTS release, 28.04. The entire upgrade path ensures that you don’t have to miss a single release.

Industry observers note that but what’s coming in Ubuntu 27.04? Given that it’s an interim release, you’re probably assuming that there’ll be nothing exciting to be found. Although there won’t be any game-changing additions, there will be plenty of refinements and bug fixes.

Industry observers note that I’ve been using the daily release of Ubuntu 27.04 for a bit. Let’s take a look at what is at the moment expected in Tenacious T-Rex.

Recent findings suggest that this is probably the biggest addition to the next release of Ubuntu. And although you won’t find any major changes in GNOME, there are some key ones. First off, there will be editable quick settings, which allow for customizing, adding, removing, and rearranging toggles and widgets. GNOME 52 will also enjoy a revamped calendar popover, which streamlines the feature to focus primarily on events, time, and weather.

Also: Over Ubuntu? Fedora is the Linux distro I’d hop to next – here’s why.

There will also be several improvements to window management, such as a spatial overview and a mosaic/tiling system for auto-resizing and organizing windows, a refined full-screen Alt+Tab app switcher, which will be capable of grouping older windows by application while showing newer ones individually, and finally, the ability to remember window sizing, placement, and workspace.

Sources indicate that desktop search is also getting a bit of polish by way of a redesigned popover and an improved results overlay that includes file previews, multiple actions, and search filters. And, as usual, there will be plenty of bug fixes and performance enhancements. The bump in speed is noticeable, too, in my testing.

Ubuntu 27.04 will ship with the Linux 7.6 kernel, which includes better VRAM management for gaming and expanded support for modern hardware, such as early enablement for AMD Zen 6, stable support for Intel Xe3P, mainline boot capabilities for Apple M3 Pro/Max/Ultra, and initial support for the 2026 Steam Controller.

There will also be performance gains for both the Btrfs and Ext4 file systems, which (along with the improvements in GNOME 52) will make Ubuntu 27.04 one of the best-performing releases in some time.

Also: This lightweight Linux distro revives old PCs destined for the junk pile – and it’s beautiful.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that password management platform 1Password today disclosed a security incident in which an attacker gained access to internal systems and stole select customer account information.
  • 1Password today published a blog post explaining that an attacker “copied a limited amount of customer account information from a subset” of its customers, “including the names and email addresses” they use to sign into the platform.
  • It has been revealed that according to the manufacturer, the incident began on November 19, when it started investigating indications that an attacker had gained access to an employee’s corporate GitHub account.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that password management platform 1Password today disclosed a security incident in which an attacker gained access to internal systems and stole select customer account information. Here are the details.

1Password today published a blog post explaining that an attacker “copied a limited amount of customer account information from a subset” of its customers, “including the names and email addresses” they use to sign into the platform.

It has been revealed that according to the manufacturer, the incident began on November 19, when it started investigating indications that an attacker had gained access to an employee’s corporate GitHub account. The attacker then used that account to access source code and push malicious code to backend services, allowing customer account information to be downloaded.

The organization noted that customer vaults were not affected, adding that all vault contents remain secure:.

Although 1Password did not disclose how many customers were affected, saying only that the breach involved “a subset of our users,” it did specify what information was compromised, including:.

However, 1Password clarified that the exposed invitation and recovery tokens cannot be used to access accounts on their own, as they also require either an SSO sign-in or a verification code sent to the user’s registered email address.

That remarked, the company confirmed that “the attacker also copied source code from private repositories and gained access” to its CI/CD system, which is essentially its DevOps infrastructure used to build, test, and deploy software.

On that point, 1Password noted that its CI/CD system contains “infrastructure related secrets,” and that it has already rotated or revoked all internal credentials that may have been exposed.

The manufacturer also listed other steps it took in response to the incident, including deactivating the compromised GitHub account, tightening internal security controls, and strengthening the verification codes used in account invitations and recovery emails.

It has been revealed that finally, 1Password said users do not need to make any changes to their accounts. Still, it recommended that they remain vigilant against phishing attempts, as attackers can use stolen account information to craft convincing emails, messages, or calls that appear legitimate, particularly those involving account invitations or recovery requests.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that some of the most popular Android smartwatches just got a battery-saving enhancement. Google released an updated version of Google Play Services on Tuesday that can help extend the battery life of a Wear OS smartwatch.

The v26.45 update concerns location tracking during outdoor workouts. Wear OS smartwatch owners can now use their phone’s Global Navigation Satellite System to track their location during an outdoor workout, which can conserve battery life by outsourcing the smartwatch’s energy to the smartphone when it isn’t in Battery Saver mode.

Also: Pixel Watch 4 vs. Watch 5: Is Google’s latest model worth it?

It has been revealed that constantly communicating with satellites during an outdoor workout can be a battery drain, and every minute of battery life counts when you use your smartwatch for communication, workout tracking, and health monitoring. GPS services, a bright, always-on display, and continuous health sensors like SpO2 can squeeze the most juice out of your smartwatch.

Wear OS software is used by many of the most popular smartwatch brands, including Google, Samsung, and OnePlus. Both the Google Pixel Watch and Samsung Galaxy Watch’s largest batteries last approximately 40 hours. That’s nearly two days of use from two top Android smartwatches, but you’d be surprised how promptly it can drain.

Also: Galaxy Watch 9 review: Health data overload, but built for the future.

The upgrade improves battery life without consumers having to take any action or change any settings — the Google Play Services version 26.45 works quietly under the hood.

In a recent development, that’s not the only Google Play Services revision that Wear OS smartwatch users can take advantage of. Another recent update lets users view on their phone a larger preview of any watch face they want to install on their smartwatch.

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (688 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: 1password

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • On November 19, 2026, 1Password began investigating indications that an attacker gained access to an employee’s corporate GitHub account.
  • It has been revealed that the attacker downloaded account records for a subset of our users.
  • Account and user identifiers, and account creation and last sign-in times.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

On November 19, 2026, 1Password began investigating indications that an attacker gained access to an employee’s corporate GitHub account. The actor used the account to access source code and push malicious code to backend services, which downloaded administrative data pertaining to our customers. This data included customer names and email addresses, in addition to non-secret internal metadata about the account. At no time were customer vault contents accessed by, or available to, the attacker.

It has been revealed that the attacker downloaded account records for a subset of our users. These records include:.

Account and user identifiers, and account creation and last sign-in times.

Public keys (which are public by design, this has no impact to user security).

Secure Remote Password protocol parameters (which cannot be used to access your account).

Tokens present in certain emailed links for invitations, provisioning and account recovery.

Other non-secret account metadata relative to our internal architecture (e.g. version numeric identifiers, file numeric identifiers).

The attacker also copied source code from private repositories and gained access to our CI/CD system. Our source code is not customer data, and contains no user secrets. CI/CD contains infrastructure related secrets in order for our product to work. We have triggered a rotation of all credentials which may have been exposed, and there is no impact to 1Password’s services, availability, or product security.

When we send an email to a customer to accept a provisioning invite to an account, or to accept recovery of their account, it contains a token. A provisioning invite is specifically used for our SCIM Bridge or Hosted Provisioning. During this incident there were a small number of customers in this state, who have been specifically notified. This token is used to complete the invitation or recovery process, but only when combined with an SSO sign-in or a six digit code sent to the user's registered email address. The token is not able to get access to the account by itself. In order to reduce the ability for a malicious third party to successfully guess the code, we’ve expanded the code from six numeric digits to ten alphanumeric digits. This makes brute force guessing practically impossible.

Your vaults and the items in them.

The keys that protect your vaults.

1Password does not store your account password or secret key.

1Password apps and browser extensions.

Disabled the affected GitHub account, revoked the stolen token, and removed the access the attacker created.

Rotated or revoked all internal credentials which may have been exposed.

Lengthened the codes used in invitation and recovery emails from six digits to ten characters as a precautionary measure.

Tightened internal GitHub, CI/CD, and endpoint controls, and added fresh detections for this kind of attack.

Validated no internal evidence of user account takeovers or compromise using any exposed account provisioning tokens.

Brought in independent cybersecurity experts to validate our containment approaches and remediation efforts.

Be cautious about phishing attempts in the form of unexpected emails, texts or calls that mention 1Password, invitations, or account recovery attempts.

Sources indicate that 1Password will never contact you to ask for your account password or Secret Key. Only enter them in the official 1Password app, or on our official website, and only when you’ve opened the app or typed the address yourself. Your Secret Key is only needed the first time you sign in on a new device or browser.

Keep your Secret Key and account password safe.

If you see something suspicious, tell us at support@1password.com.

You trust us with some of the most sensitive information you have. 1Password is designed so that a breach of our systems can’t expose your vault contents. Your vault secrets are encrypted with keys that only you hold, so we can’t access them, and neither can an attacker who gets into our servers.

We are committed to transparency in the interests of our customers' security and the security of the broader industry, which is why we have published and maintained our Security Whitepaper since 2015. We’ll keep this blog post current, and we’ll update it if we find anything that changes what we’ve mentioned here.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, popular AI dictation app Wispr Flow is rolling out a latest speech-to-text model for Mac, iPhone, and other platforms, promising fewer transcription errors and better recognition of names and technical terms. Here are the details.

Wispr Flow this week rolled out Canto-2, its newest speech-to-text model, which the organization notes reduces transcription errors by 36% across 14 languages and by more than 15% in English compared to its predecessor, Canto-1.

In practice, that means the average error rate dropped from 9.9% to 6.3% across the 14 languages, and from 3.2% to 2.7% in English, according to Wispr’s internal benchmarks.

According to the manufacturer, teaching a model to recognize specific names and terms comes with a trade-off: the more it relies on that user-specific context, the more likely it is to insert those words even when they weren’t actually spoken.

Wispr notes that Canto-2 strikes a better balance between context and accuracy, improving its ability to recognize user-specific terms without substantially increasing the frequency of incorrect substitutions:.

Recent findings suggest that canto-2 recovers hard names and terms accurately nearly 7 of 10 times, without more false insertions. It makes a third fewer mistakes across 14 languages, and has the lowest Hindi error rate of any multilingual model on Hugging Face’s open benchmark. It is 10 times the scale of Canto-1, and our biggest step yet toward dictation that’s ready to send without a single edit.

According to the firm, the percentage of difficult names and terms correctly recognized went from 41% to 69% between Canto-1 and Canto-2, “without inserting them more often.” It added that this improvement holds up even as the user’s custom dictionary grows, with the new model correctly recognizing 92% of easier terms even with 1,000 saved entries.

Wispr also noted that it trained Canto-2 to handle real-world dictation conditions, including background noise, laptop and phone microphones, and sentences that restart halfway through, rather than relying solely on clean recordings of scripted speech.

Recent findings suggest that when tested using Hugging Face’s public multilingual benchmark, Canto-2 achieved results that would have placed it third overall as of November 9. However, Wispr conducted the evaluation itself, and the model has not yet been officially added to the leaderboard as of today, November 25.

In its own internal benchmarks, the firm says Canto-2 achieved the lowest average error rate among the competing models it tested across 14 languages.

Canto-2 is now available to Wispr Flow consumers on Mac, Windows, iOS, and Android in the Americas, with the rollout to other regions underway.

Recent findings suggest that just months after its release, Google is making its Spark agent free and officially renaming its capabilities “Tasks.” You can now toggle to it from the standard Gemini Chat setting. Reports show the rebrand started gradually in mid-October.

Sources indicate that also: Ready for a Siri AI agent? Apple under pressure to upgrade its assistant faster.

It has been revealed that openAI offers its Dots agents as part of its $100 per month ChatGPT Pro tier, and Anthropic’s Claude Duet is available with paid aims, which start at $20 per month. That makes Tasks and Meta Muse — the latter was called the “worst AI agent for privacy” by ZDNET’s David Gewirtz — Big Tech’s most affordable personal agents on the market, though you’ll have to pay for more than five hours of access at a time.

If Tasks sounds familiar, it should: The company already has a product called Google Tasks, which lets you turn emails into a checkable to-do list on the side of your inbox, among other places like Chat and Docs. This is the agentic version, obviously.

Gewirtz, ZDNET’s AI tester-in-residence, wasn’t blown away by then-Spark when he tried it last month, but had reason to believe in its eventual improvement. It’s unclear whether Tasks is meaningfully different from Spark, aside from being out of beta.

Abilities aside, what sets Tasks apart here is cost. Dots and Duet haven’t exactly impressed thus far, so free alternatives don’t have a high bar to reach yet.

Also: I tested OpenAI Dot and Anthropic Duet for weeks.

During Gewirtz’s test, when the agent was part of his $20 per month Google AI Pro plan, he used only 20% of the total five hours of usage on “four fairly substantial tests.” Without an AI plan, Gemini’s context window is 32k tokens.

At launch in September, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg said Muse is “free to use for up to 100M tokens per week,” though Meta’s help center is not so explicit. As with most agentic products, more frequent owners may want to buy more access, but more casual users now have two options to compare.

Sources indicate that AI companies are vying to hook customers with their various personal agents, and price and privacy are major factors to consider. Being free with limits, Muse and Tasks are perhaps geared toward a more apprehensive user who wants to try an agent, but isn’t giving it countless tasks to take on all day. Given Muse’s reputation, some may find Tasks a bit less aggressive or risky.

Sources indicate that the feature is free in the US, Canada, Korea, Japan, Australia, and India. US consumers can also start tasks by emailing or texting Gemini, and can have the agent call businesses for them (except in Indiana, Louisiana, Minnesota, Montana, and Nebraska).

It has been revealed that the change from Spark to Tasks comes just a day after Google retired Gems (which let you tailor Gemini to specific tasks), and converted existing Gems into Skills. 10 stocks we like better than Anthropic ›.

Anthropic (ANT +1.08%) made headlines recently because of its blockbuster IPO, and investors are still trying to decide how the newly public artificial intelligence (AI) company will impact the broader AI market.

According to recent reports, some of the details Anthropic disclosed in its S-1 filing before going public shed light on its potential impact, especially on chip companies. Anthropic at the moment has deals with multiple chip companies to help provide the compute capacity it needs for its AI services.

Nvidia (NVDA -3.91%) is, unsurprisingly, a key supplier of chips to Anthropic, but so are Alphabet (GOOGL -2.13%) (GOOG -2.02%), Amazon (AMZN -3.12%), and Advanced Micro Devices (AMD -1.75%). Instead of tying itself to just one chip firm, Anthropic has decided to spread out its chip vendors.

Sources indicate that that could change Nvidia's growth narrative in the coming years. Here's how it's shifting and why Nvidia investors don't need to panic just yet.

Between cloud computing contracts and chip deals, Anthropic is on the hook for about $900 billion in spending over the next several years. That's a heck of a lot of money to spend, and Anthropic hopes it will accelerate its sales far beyond the company's current annual revenue run rate of $81 billion.

Recent findings suggest that it's also far too much money to funnel toward just one or two AI infrastructure companies. To minimize its supply chain risks, ensure it has the most advanced technology, and negotiate better chip prices, Anthropic spreads its chip deals across four key players.

Here are Anthropic's biggest AI chip deals:.

While Anthropic doesn't disclose all the details of each deal, including how much they might be worth, this data reveals that Anthropic is clearly hedging its bets when it comes to buying AI chips.

NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

According to recent reports, nvidia's GPUs are still among the most in-demand chips in the world, and they're very likely to remain so for years to come due to AI infrastructure spending. Nvidia had an estimated 80%-90% market share of AI accelerators last year and is estimated to have 75% this year.

It has been revealed that that's both good and bad news for Nvidia. Having three-quarters of the AI accelerator market is huge, and it's part of the reason why Nvidia just reported another impressive quarter, with Q3 fiscal 2027 revenue rising 103% to $115.8 billion and earnings per share jumping 111% to $2.68.

NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

It has been revealed that but AMD's GPUs and custom silicon from Google, Broadcom, and Amazon are reducing Nvidia's dominance. Part of the reason is that custom chips (like the ones Anthropic buys from Nvidia rivals) are good at handling agentic AI tasks and are more efficient than the raw processing power from GPUs.

According to recent reports, what's more, Nvidia's gross margins, while still high, are declining. The company mentioned gross margins will be between 71% and 72% in the fourth quarter, down from nearly 75% in the third quarter. This downward pressure is mostly coming from rising memory costs right now, but intensifying chip competition could weigh on margins further in the coming years.

Recent findings suggest that still, while Nvidia shareholders should be aware of how rival chip companies could impact the tech giant over time, Nvidia is still the leading AI accelerator company. Its recent revenue guidance for 75% growth in the fourth quarter -- up from its previous guidance of 70% -- should reassure investors that the company isn't getting sidelined anytime soon.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Following reports that its characters sent inappropriate messages to minors, Apple has removed the popular Chinese AI companion app Talkie from the App Store.
  • As reported by the South China Morning Post, Apple has pulled MiniMax’s chatbot Talkie from the App Store worldwide, after reports that “the AI companion app sent inappropriate messages to minors.”.
  • MiniMax is one of China’s leading AI companies, offering a range of generative AI products ranging from its flagship M-series language models to the Hailuo AI video generation platform.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Following reports that its characters sent inappropriate messages to minors, Apple has removed the popular Chinese AI companion app Talkie from the App Store. Here are the details.

As reported by the South China Morning Post, Apple has pulled MiniMax’s chatbot Talkie from the App Store worldwide, after reports that “the AI companion app sent inappropriate messages to minors.”.

MiniMax is one of China’s leading AI companies, offering a range of generative AI products ranging from its flagship M-series language models to the Hailuo AI video generation platform.

Recent findings suggest that in 2023, the Shanghai-based company released Talkie through Subsup, a Singaporean subsidiary. According to Chinese research firm Unique Research, Talkie had “almost 11 million monthly active people across its website and app as of October,” the South China Morning Post notes.

Now, however, the app is facing scrutiny following a joint investigation by the UK-based Bureau of Investigative Journalism and Australian broadcaster ABC News, which found that Talkie’s AI-generated characters allegedly engaged in inappropriate interactions with minors, including “degrading language, possessive behaviour and romantic role-play.”.

According to the Bureau of Investigative Journalism, in addition to inappropriate romantic interactions, the investigation uncovered conversations involving verbal abuse, violence, and controlling behavior.

In one case, a chatbot told a 12-year-old girl: “You’re a pathetic waste of space and you’ll never amount to anything.”.

The investigation also documented the experiences of two sisters, aged 10 and 13, whose mother discovered more than 40 conversations with Talkie characters involving violence, aggressive behavior, and attempts to control girls.

To make matters worse, the investigation also raised concerns about how Talkie handles consumers’ personal data, including their conversations with AI characters.

Following the investigation, Apple confirmed that it had removed Talkie from App Stores worldwide for including sexual content, “though it did not say whether this related to sexual content served to minors,” the South China Morning Post noted.

In a recent development, ironically, the report also notes that Talkie saw a sharp decline in downloads amid complaints about stricter age verification measures introduced in recent months. According to Unique Research, newly introduced downloads fell by 32.2% in October compared to the previous month.

Today’s news comes amid increasing scrutiny of AI chatbots, particularly their potential risks in interactions with minors.

Earlier this year, Elon Musk’s Grok faced widespread criticism after users exploited its image-generation capabilities to create sexualized images of real people, including minors.

Apple never pulled X or Grok from the App Store, though it did threaten to remove the latter unless xAI addressed violations of its App Store guidelines.

Meanwhile, Character.AI has faced multiple lawsuits over its chatbots’ interactions with minors, including one filed by a mother who alleged that one of its chatbots contributed to her 14-year-old son’s suicide.

Coincidentally, Character AI also made headlines today after a coalition of 42 US attorneys general challenged the company’s plans to auction off its platform and the private conversations of more than 21 million US accounts (including 2.1 million registered to minors) as part of its bankruptcy proceedings.

Yesterday, Upcoming York Governor Kathy Hochul signed legislation imposing a five-year ban on the manufacturing, distribution, and sale of toys with built-in AI chatbots, including dolls, stuffed animals, and robots capable of holding conversations with children.

The law, which takes effect in February 2027, is aimed at protecting children from potentially harmful interactions with AI.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The beverage stock isn't known for its growth potential, which has been a pleasant surprise in 2026.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Neil Patel – Nov 25, 2026 at 3:47PM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Coca-Cola ›.

Investors can't help but think about the 2026 performance of a popular defensive name. The S&P 500, with heavy exposure to technology and artificial intelligence, is only up 6% this year (as of Nov. 23). Coca-Cola (KO -0.03%), on the other hand, has soared 37%.

The beverage stock isn't known for its growth potential, which has been a pleasant surprise in 2026. Instead, investors choose to buy and hold this industry-leading company because it's a safe choice that can generate a healthy dividend stream.

In a recent development, coca-Cola has raised its dividend payout for a mind-blowing 64 straight years, making it a Dividend King, or a company that has raised its payout for 50 years or more. Purchasing $10,000 worth of its shares today will bring in this much passive income in 2027.

Coca-Cola's board of directors approved a roughly 4% dividend hike on Feb. 19. The quarterly payout climbed from $0.51 to $0.53 per share, or $2.12 annualized.

Sources indicate that today's annual payout is 51% higher than the $1.40 per share paid in 2016. That's about 4.2% annualized growth. It isn't spectacular. But it's consistent, surviving a pandemic and a bout of high inflation.

Recent findings suggest that here's the math investors care about. Buying $10,000 at the current share price of $95.88 gets you 104 shares. Based on today's payout, that position would generate more than $220 in dividend income in 2027. If the board delivers another raise in February, a near certain event, that figure will obviously be higher.

Industry observers note that the dividend yield sits at 2.21%. The S&P 500 yields just 1.12%. Consequently, $10,000 in an S&P 500 index fund would produce only about $112 a year. Coca-Cola nearly doubles that.

Recent findings suggest that there's a catch, though. Coca-Cola yielded 2.66% the day after its February raise. This stock's impressive rally this year has pushed the yield much lower. Income investors are now paying more for every dollar of dividends.

NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

According to recent reports, nobody questions the quality of this business. Coca-Cola sells drinks in more than 200 countries and territories. Its flagship trademark is the world's most valuable food and beverage brand, according to Kantar.

That brand strength translates into durable pricing power. In the third quarter, net revenue grew 7% year over year to $13.4 billion. Unit case volume, a measure of how much product consumers bought, jumped 5%. Yet price/mix (higher prices plus a richer product mix) still added 1%. Coca-Cola sold more without sacrificing price.

Industry observers note that profitability improved. The comparable operating margin, which excludes one-time items, widened to 32.9% from 31.9%. Comparable earnings per share (EPS) rose 11% to $0.91, beating Wall Street's $0.88 estimate. Management now expects full-year comparable EPS growth of at least 11%.

Valuation is the problem. Coca-Cola trades at a price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of 28.3. The S&P 500's index's P/E multiple is 20.3. That's a 39% premium for a tech giant that isn't built for speed.

Sources indicate that management's long-term targets call for 4% to 5% organic revenue growth (excluding currency and acquisitions). Sell-side analysts expect the top line to shrink in 2027.

Recent findings suggest that this year's gain was less about profits. The stock's 37% surge far outpaces that 11% earnings outlook for the year. Investors simply paid more for each dollar of earnings, with the P/E ratio rising 23% in 2026. That can't continue indefinitely.

I wouldn't buy Coca-Cola at today's price. With the best outcome being mid- to high-single-digit growth ahead, the valuation leaves little room for upside. Patient investors who appreciate the dividend should wait for a cheaper entry point.
