The FCC Approved a Million SpaceX Satellites for Data Centers in Space

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (586 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Federal Communications Commission has approved SpaceX’s request to launch 1 million AI-equipped satellites to create vast data centers in space.
  • Recent findings suggest that spaceX initially filed an application in May asking for permission to launch the satellites, collectively known as Starmind.
  • “It’s just really abrogating their responsibility to go, ‘Well, this is a project they’re proposing.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Federal Communications Commission has approved SpaceX’s request to launch 1 million AI-equipped satellites to create vast data centers in space.

Recent findings suggest that spaceX initially filed an application in May asking for permission to launch the satellites, collectively known as Starmind. The FCC’s approval requires that SpaceX launch its first data center satellite by 2030 and meet the 1 million mark by 2040.

“It’s just really abrogating their responsibility to go, ‘Well, this is a project they’re proposing. Is this actually safe?’” Jonathan McDowell, an astrophysicist who tracks satellite launches, told CNET. “It’s a blank check. Launch as many satellites as you can, and we’ll just see what happens. I think this is a mistake on the FCC’s part.”.

Orbital data centers have long been a goal of SpaceX CEO Elon Musk, becoming a pivotal part of his pitch to investors ahead of the manufacturer’s IPO in June.

“You’re power-constrained on Earth. Space has the advantage that it’s always sunny,” Musk remarked in March.

On its web page for Starmind, SpaceX touts its high-efficiency solar arrays on the planned satellites and the cooling benefits of space. It claims that high-speed laser links will beam the AI results back to Earth through Starlink’s constellation.

Space experts I’ve talked to this year about Starmind have been skeptical. The technical challenges alone are dizzying; the scale of SpaceX’s ambitions is hard to swallow.

It’s taken seven years for Starlink to grow its constellation to 11,195 satellites, and that was already an unprecedented feat. Is it possible to get to 1 million satellites in 14 years?

“We do not have the launch capacity for any of this,” Ian Christensen, senior director at the Secure World Foundation, told me in a previous interview. “Not even within SpaceX to do their own constellation, let alone the other constellations planned.”.

SpaceX has increasingly prioritized launching its own satellites instead of letting commercial customers hitch a ride on their rockets. Starlink’s share of SpaceX missions has gone from 54% of its Falcon 9 rocket’s missions in 2020 to about 79% in 2026, according to a Reuters analysis. One analysis estimates that SpaceX would have to launch 5,000 Starship rockets a year to meet its goal — a staggering increase from 330 rockets that launched last year in total.

Scientists have already been ringing alarm bells about overcrowded orbits as they exist now. The more satellites in space, the more difficult it is for operators to maneuver around each other. A single crash could turn into decades of orbital debris, which could cause a chain reaction that eventually makes space inoperable for everyone. And burning up all those satellites in the atmosphere when they reach the end of their lives has already started to leave ozone-depleting aluminum particles behind. A paper published this week in Earth and Space Chemistry estimated that SpaceX’s data center plan would multiply pollutants in the upper atmosphere by more than 150 times compared to last year.

“There are scientific papers out there raising issues,” McDowell said. “Yes, they’re unproven, but if I say, ‘Yeah, we’re not sure if this is going to destroy the atmosphere and kill us all, but it might,’ is the right reaction to go, ‘Well, you haven’t proven it, so we’re just going to ignore it’?”.

The FCC’s approval came despite objections from Amazon, the environmental nonprofit Public Employees for Environmental Responsibility and the American Astronomical Society.

A representative for SpaceX did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Etihad Guest, the loyalty program of Abu Dhabi-based Etihad Airways, is expanding its U.S. presence by introducing two fresh credit cards. Most people won’t get much value from these cards, but they can make sense for Etihad frequent flyers who want elite status.

The two cards are the Etihad Guest Visa Signature® Card ($99 annual fee) and the Etihad Guest Premier Visa Signature® Card ($499 annual fee). Issued by the First National Bank of Omaha, both offer faster pathways to earning and maintaining elite status and the ability to earn extra miles on Etihad purchases.

They also offer extra miles on international transactions (neither has foreign transaction fees) and purchases with Etihad’s partner airlines, which include U.S. carriers like American Airlines and JetBlue Airways.

Here’s what you need to know about the cards.

The Etihad Guest Visa Signature® Card comes with a $99 annual fee, and it earns Etihad Guest miles at the following rates:.

3 miles per $1 spent on Etihad purchases.

2 miles per $1 spent on Etihad partner airline purchases.

Recent findings suggest that 2 miles per $1 spent on non-U.S. purchases.

1 mile per $1 spent on all other U.S. purchases.

It has been revealed that welcome offer: Through Feb. 3, 2027, the card is offering the following welcome offer for new applicants: Earn up to 40,000 welcome Etihad Guest Miles, including 10,000 miles after the first purchase and an additional 30,000 miles after spending $3,000 within the first three billing cycles after account opening.

It has been revealed that elite status benefits: You’ll also get Etihad Silver status after your first Etihad purchase within 90 days of opening your account. Unlike most airlines, that entry-level status is enough to get you into the business class lounge when traveling through Etihad’s hub at Abu Dhabi’s Zayed International Airport.

You can retain that status by spending $20,000 a year on the card, or $3,000 a year on Etihad purchases.

The Etihad Guest Premier Visa Signature® Card comes with a $499 annual fee, and it earns Etihad Guest miles at the following rates:.

5 miles per $1 spent on Etihad purchases.

3 miles per $1 spent on Etihad partner airline purchases.

It has been revealed that 2 miles per $1 spent on non-U.S. purchases.

1 mile per $1 spent on all other U.S. purchases.

The only differences in rewards between the premium and standard cards are increased earning rates for eligible airline purchases.

It has been revealed that welcome offer: Through Feb. 3, 2027, the premium card offers a higher welcome offer compared to the standard card: Earn up to 60,000 welcome Etihad Guest Miles, including 20,000 miles after the first purchase and 40,000 miles after spending $7,000 within the first three billing cycles after account opening.

Elite status benefits: The premium card offers a faster track to elite status: automatic Silver status upon card approval and Gold status after your first Etihad purchase within 90 days of opening your account.

In a recent development, to maintain Gold status, you’ll need to spend $40,000 a year on the card, or $8,000 on Etihad purchases. Otherwise, you’ll have Silver status.

According to recent reports, wi-Fi benefit: After your first Etihad purchase, you’ll get 3,000 Etihad Guest miles, enough to cover Wi-Fi costs on a long-haul Etihad flight. You’ll then get those miles again after each cardholder anniversary.

Industry observers note that travel benefits: The card offers a statement credit for Global Entry or TSA PreCheck and select travel protections. If you already have a premium travel card, you might already have access to these perks.

The card also includes a Priority Pass lounge access membership. However, an Etihad spokesperson told NerdWallet that it’s the entry-level membership tier, so you’ll need to pay for yourself and guests each time you visit a Priority Pass lounge. Most premium credit cards in the U.S. that offer Priority Pass allow complimentary visits for at least the cardholder.

The Etihad cards make the most sense for Etihad’s frequent flyers who are flying to or connecting through Abu Dhabi several times a year.

That’s because the standard card’s accelerated pathway to Etihad Guest’s Silver status tier can unlock the ability to choose business class lounge access in Abu Dhabi as a status perk.

In a recent development, with the premium card, you get a fast track to Gold. If you select lounge access as a Gold status perk, you can not only bring a guest on the same flight into the lounge, but also access Etihad’s worldwide lounge network. That includes Etihad’s own lounges in Upcoming York and Washington, D.C., as well as most partner lounges at other Etihad destinations.

Bear in mind that while Etihad has many partnerships with other airlines, it’s not part of an alliance, so you don’t get lounge benefits when traveling on partners. You’ll need to be flying on an Etihad-operated flight to get into the lounge.

If you primarily fly with other carriers, then Etihad status will have limited upside for you.

However, the Priority Pass lounge membership that comes with the premium card does not have that restriction. You can access Priority Pass lounges while flying on any airline, although you’ll need to pay an additional per-person $35 fee each visit.

Sources indicate that the earning rates on the Etihad cards are lackluster for everyday spenders. The bonus categories are for airline purchases with Etihad and its partners, as well as international spending.

That means your day-to-day purchases at home, like groceries, dining out and gas, earn only 1 mile per $1 spent.

It has been revealed that plus, there are more ways to earn Etihad Guest miles than spending on an Etihad credit card. For example, you can transfer points to Etihad Guest from Bilt Rewards, Capital One and Citi ThankYou.

It has been revealed that those programs offer cards that typically have better benefits and bonus categories, and they offer flexibility on how you can use your points and miles. With an Etihad card, you can only earn Etihad Guest miles, which expire after 18 months without qualifying flight activity. (If you’re not traveling on Etihad or its partners at least once every 18 months, then you definitely should not get the cards.).

One of the most interesting perks of the fresh cards is the bonus category for spending with Etihad partner airlines — 2 miles per $1 for the standard card and 3 miles per $1 for the premium version. Typically, airline credit cards reward customers only for spending on the airline, not partners.

Sources indicate that there are better cards available, though. Some offer as many or even more points per $1 on flights purchased directly from airlines.

If you want the card solely to earn more Etihad Guest miles, then the answer for most people is no.

While you can earn more miles for purchases with Etihad and partner airlines, the earning rates aren’t attractive enough to justify the annual fees, especially when compared with existing cards with currencies that transfer to Etihad Guest.

Status chasers could benefit from the fast track to elite status — but you would need to be a fairly frequent Etihad flyer to really take advantage of your elite benefits.

New To-Do List Item: Find Replacement for Microsoft To Do

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that if you, like me, are the type of person who makes a lot of to-do lists and can’t breathe a sigh of relief until you check items off them, I have some bad news.
  • It has been revealed that we’ve seen no announcement or acknowledgment in the app itself that To Do, which debuted in 2017, would be retired.
  • Sources indicate that microsoft To Do is retiring.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that if you, like me, are the type of person who makes a lot of to-do lists and can’t breathe a sigh of relief until you check items off them, I have some bad news. One of the best free options for organizing your work and home life is reaching the end of its life. Microsoft prepares to retire its To Do app at the end of June 2027.

It has been revealed that we’ve seen no announcement or acknowledgment in the app itself that To Do, which debuted in 2017, would be retired. But several Microsoft-watching websites this week spotted a blog post from the company recommending customers switch to its Planner app.

Sources indicate that microsoft To Do is retiring. For work or school accounts, Microsoft Planner will be the destination for managing personal work tasks alongside assigned work. The updated My tasks experience begins rolling out in December 2026.

Microsoft To Do apps will retire on June 30, 2027. This includes To Do on the web, Windows, Mac, iOS, and Android, for both work or school accounts and personal Microsoft accounts.

Recent findings suggest that the underlying To Do service, APIs, and related synchronization support will retire on separate, later timelines. We’ll communicate those dates and any required preparation separately.

Sources indicate that but there’s a big catch for Microsoft customers who are on 365 Personal or 365 Family looks: Planner will not be available to them. That means Microsoft is telling To Do users on those accounts to find a comparable app elsewhere if they’re not on a business account that includes Planner.

The change was also mentioned in a separate Microsoft post about unified tasks and aims for Copilot and Microsoft 365 from Microsoft product manager Ashna Patel.

In a statement provided to CNET, Howard Crow, director of product, agents and AI at Microsoft, mentioned the change consolidates task management across Microsoft 365. “We recognize this change will affect customers differently, particularly those using personal Microsoft accounts, and we’re committed to helping them prepare,” Crow said.

Crow noted the firm will share more information about the transition in the coming months.

According to recent reports, while the end of June 2027 may sound like a very long time from now, the path Microsoft has offered for To Do consumers is not a great one if you want to take action now. There’s no built-in export feature in the app, though in the blog post, Microsoft promises, “Microsoft will provide a way to export your To Do data before the apps retire. We’ll patch this article with instructions, supported data, requirements, and limitations when those details are finalized.”.

Already, there are some pretty severe limitations even for those on Microsoft plans that support Planner: Existing To Do list items won’t work after that June deadline. “After that date, you will no longer be able to view or manage them in Planner,” the post noted.

In the meantime, you can shop around for alternate apps, some free, including Google Keep, ToDoist and Notion.

It has been revealed that to Do users, myself included, are not happy. As Windows Latest reported, comments in response to Microsoft’s decision included, “Do you actually hate your users?”.

If this were simply a case of Microsoft creating software people didn’t like and then abandoning it, that would be one thing. But the To Do retirement is especially painful for those of us who were forced to move to Microsoft’s app a few years after it purchased Wunderlist.

Wunderlist was a German app that released in 2011 and quickly became popular for its slick interface, easy-to-upgrade task lists and its availability across web, desktop and mobile platforms. Microsoft absorbed some of Wunderlist into To Do and killed the original app in 2020 without ever offering all of the features that made Wunderlist great.

As someone who used Wunderlist for years and has been using To Do, I can tell you that while To Do has been essential in my work and personal life, it never became as intuitive to use as Wunderlist. It never handled predictive task creation as well as Wunderlist did (such as understanding as you typed the date of a task or if it was repeating). It lacked features for sharing lists or collaborating on them, and simply didn’t look as stylish. As far as aesthetics, the best thing Microsoft did with To Do was add a Dark Mode.

According to recent reports, wunderlist was a joy to use. To Do always felt like the knockoff diet version of it and never quite as good.

After several years, I simply gave up on the idea that Microsoft would improve the app or add any new features, but kept using it out of necessity given the lack of a built-in export option.

According to recent reports, the death announcement is not surprising. Just sad.

RIP To Do, but really RIP to the last remnants of Wunderlist.

  • It has been revealed that instead, it has sold off Nvidia's stock to a point not seen in years.
  • Industry observers note that however, Nvidia has grown significantly as a company since then, making its valuation cheap.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Keithen Drury – Nov 25, 2026 at 5:00PM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Nvidia ›.

Industry observers note that nvidia (NVDA -3.91%) stock has had a busy few weeks. It was heavily affected by the resignation of its co-founder and CEO, Jensen Huang, and questions are now surfacing about how much of Nvidia's sales were conducted legally and whether any of its chips ended up in China. Huang is now back as CEO, but there is no definitive answer on export issues, and the market isn't sticking around to find out the conclusion of this saga.

It has been revealed that instead, it has sold off Nvidia's stock to a point not seen in years. In fact, with its stock closing at about $125 per share on Friday, it's traded at a price not seen since May 2025. After Huang returned, the stock rose to around $155 per share. Nvidia stock hasn’t been priced this low since mid-2025.

Industry observers note that however, Nvidia has grown significantly as a company since then, making its valuation cheap. But just how cheap is it? Let's take a look.

First, let's look at how Nvidia is trading based on trailing earnings. For reference, the S&P 500 (^GSPC -0.25%) trades at 20.3 times trailing earnings. As of the price Nvidia closed at on Nov. 24, the stock trades at just 16.7 times earnings.

That type of discount is normally reserved for companies with major business problems or those operating in deeply cyclical industries. While Nvidia may operate in a cyclical industry, the reality is that the artificial intelligence build-out isn't wrapping up anytime soon, and there will always be a need to replace outdated or burnt-out equipment.

In a recent development, however, the trailing price-to-earnings ratio is a bad metric for Nvidia. Why? It's all due to the growth Nvidia will produce.

NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

In a recent development, during the organization’s fiscal third quarter of 2027 (ending Oct. 25), CFO Colette Kress raised the company’s revenue growth guidance for fiscal 2028 from 70% to 75%. That's an impressive figure considering how quickly Nvidia grew this year, and if those growth figures hold up, the stock will be even cheaper.

Nvidia now trades for just 9.3 times next year's earnings.

NVDA PE Ratio (Forward 1y) data by YCharts.

So, what's a fair value for Nvidia? If you think it's about 30 times trailing earnings, then if Nvidia rises to that level and hits next year's estimates, the stock could triple. A lot would need to go right with investigations, but it's not out of the question, either.

Recent findings suggest that while there are many unknowns about Nvidia's future, there are also many known factors. The AI boom isn't slowing down for anyone or anything, and that could lead to incredible performance over the next few years. I think now is the perfect time to buy Nvidia stock, as its price is driven more by fear than by reality.

We Shot a Ship Into an Asteroid to See if It Would Move. See the First Images of the Impact

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (921 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Five years ago, NASA launched its DART spacecraft with the express intent of ramming it into Dimorphos, an asteroid orbiting the larger Didymos asteroid, to see if its trajectory could be changed.
  • The ESA livestreamed the presentation on Tuesday to the delight of cosmic rubberneckers everywhere.
  • It has been revealed that at the time of the mission, the only instruments that could see the impact and the massive cloud of debris flying off Dimorphos were the Hubble Space Telescope and multiple telescopes on Earth.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Five years ago, NASA launched its DART spacecraft with the express intent of ramming it into Dimorphos, an asteroid orbiting the larger Didymos asteroid, to see if its trajectory could be changed. The mission was a success, making Dimorphos the first celestial object whose orbit was moved by humans. And now, the European Space Agency has published images showing the damage the mission caused to the asteroid.

The ESA livestreamed the presentation on Tuesday to the delight of cosmic rubberneckers everywhere. The images shown during the livestream were captured by the ESA’s Hera, which was introduced in October 2024 and spent two years in deep space with its two CubeSats to measure, map, probe and eventually land on the asteroid.

It has been revealed that at the time of the mission, the only instruments that could see the impact and the massive cloud of debris flying off Dimorphos were the Hubble Space Telescope and multiple telescopes on Earth. But they were unable to get a good enough view to see how much damage it did to the asteroid or any other potential changes that occurred.

This means that researchers had to estimate the damage until Hera showed scientists exactly what happened. Spoiler: All of those estimates were incorrect, and by a wide margin.

Hera demonstrated the damage was vastly more significant than originally thought. Scientists believed the impact would generate a 20-meter crater; Hera found that almost the entire end of the asteroid had been blown off, resulting in a crater the size of a football stadium and as wide as Dimorphos itself. This is visible in the above image — as you can see, Dimorphos used to be roughly the shape of an egg. Now, it’s the shape of a deviled egg or a kidney bean, depending on which angle you view it from.

The ESA’s Hera team discovered another neat effect of the impact: Before DART crashed into the asteroid, it was tidally locked to Didymos, much like the moon is to Earth. Scientists expected it to stay that way after the impact, but the images from Hera confirmed that Dimorphos now tumbles randomly, which none of the researchers had on their bingo card.

“Before the DART impact, Dimorphos has always shown its same face to Didymos,” said ESA Hera Mission Specialist Michael Kueppers during the presentation. “And this is what we see now. You can see it looks for a few seconds in the video like regular rotation, but it’s spinning around completely crazy.”.

ESA mission manager Ian Carnelli said this surprise was great news because it’ll allow Hera to view Dimorphos on all of its sides, which would have been challenging if it were still tidally locked to Didymos.

The ESA concluded the stream with one final surprise. According to Hera principal investigator Patrick Michel, the Hera team told engineers that it was entirely safe to go to Dimorphos because all the debris would be ejected from the DART impact, with the remaining bits reabsorbed by Didymos and Dimorphos before Hera arrived.

Industry observers note that but there is actually quite a lot of debris around the two asteroids. Kueppers says they’ve identified over 100 boulders so far, marked as white dots in the image above. Despite being completely wrong about the debris field, the Hera team was in good spirits since this means there are more things for the team to study.

Sources indicate that kueppers claims scientists are “always happy” either way because when they predict something correctly, they get awarded, and when they predict something wrong, they have a challenge to solve. “The problem is for the engineers,” he said.

It has been revealed that the three discoveries were made just 20 days into Hera’s mission, which is slated to last six months. The Hera team remarked more images and discoveries are coming in the next half year.

The point of the DART mission was to see whether humans could deal with a potentially dangerous asteroid by ramming into it or destroying it, as is often seen in Hollywood films like Deep Impact and Armageddon. NASA even frames it as a “planetary defense test.”.

Sources indicate that the mission was considered an overwhelming success. NASA was hoping to shorten the orbit of Dimorphos by at least 73 seconds, with the most optimal guess being approximately 10 minutes. The orbit was shortened by 33 minutes and 15 seconds. It was such a large discrepancy that scientists studied it and determined that the large amount of debris created extra recoil that amplified the push.

In a recent development, the change in orbit around Didymos also changed the orbit of both asteroids around the sun by about 11.7 microns per second. This doesn’t seem significant, but it adds up to about 1 kilometer every 2.7 years. This is enough to steer potential city-killer asteroids away from Earth’s orbit, given enough time and a substantial enough battering ram.

Hera’s findings also show the impact was much more devastating than scientists first thought. This provides even more data for NASA and the ESA to work through to proposal for such an event if it ever happens.

“As upcoming data come in each day, astronomers will be able to better assess whether, and how, a mission like DART could be used in the future to help protect Earth from a collision with an asteroid if we ever discover one headed our way,” said Lori Glaze, director of NASA’s Planetary Science Division, in a statement from 2022.

Strands, the New York Times' elevated word-search game, requires the player to perform a twist on the classic word search. Words can be made from linked letters — up, down, left, right, or diagonal, but words can also change direction, resulting in quirky shapes and patterns. Every single letter in the grid will be part of an answer. There's always a theme linking every solution, along with the "spangram," a special, word or phrase that sums up that day's theme, and spans the entire grid horizontally or vertically.

By providing an opaque hint and not providing the word list, Strands creates a brain-teasing game that takes a little longer to play than its other games, like Wordle and Connections.

Tech Report: What Is a Reconditioning Fee on a Used Car?

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that A reconditioning fee is an added dealer charge you might find when buying a used car.
  • The reconditioning process varies between dealerships, but typically includes these steps:.
  • An auto tech does a quick walk-around the vehicle and notes any corrosion, damage or wear.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that A reconditioning fee is an added dealer charge you might find when buying a used car. It’s intended to cover any costs the dealer incurs to make sure a used car is showroom-ready, from mechanical inspections to detailing.

The reconditioning process varies between dealerships, but typically includes these steps:.

A visual exterior inspection. An auto tech does a quick walk-around the vehicle and notes any corrosion, damage or wear.

An interior inspection. The engine and auto interior are examined and tested, and any concerns are documented.

A test drive. The car is taken out for a drive to check that it runs well and that the radio, brakes, A/C and other components are all functioning properly.

In a recent development, service and repair. Any interior or exterior mechanical, functional or cosmetic issues that were found are repaired, including paint, dents, oil changes and major engine work.

Sources indicate that inspection. Once repairs are completed, the car is inspected again to make sure everything looks and functions as it should.

Sources indicate that detailing. This includes deep interior, engine and exterior cleaning as well as any necessary leather refurbishing, bumper repair or wheel restoration.

Industry observers note that reconditioning fees are legal, but that doesn’t mean you have to pay them. Dealers can charge whatever they want for a reconditioning fee, and it’s not uncommon to find them ranging from around $500 to over $2,000.

It has been revealed that the good news: Reconditioning fees, like most dealer extras, can be negotiable. Ask the dealer for a breakdown of the reconditioning fee to see what kind of work was done to prepare the car for sale. If the work was minor but the fee is high — for example, if they’re asking for $1,995 but replaced the floor mats only — that’s a good sign it’s a bogus charge.

Sources indicate that however, when it comes time for negotiation, don’t just haggle over the reconditioning fee or other individual fees. The best way to negotiate is to focus on the out-the-door price, or the total amount you’re paying for the car. This simplifies the negotiation process and keeps you focused on the true price of your car.

All dealers invest some amount in reconditioning, but those costs are often built into the dealer’s asking price for a vehicle, rather than as a separate charge.

Some dealers opt to add a reconditioning fee to the bill because it allows them to advertise a lower asking price online, which doesn’t include fees. It’s a tactic to get you into their dealership, since the asking price is lower than that of other dealerships.

However, once you arrive, you may find that the out-the-door price is the same — or more — compared with what other dealers are asking.

Sources indicate that some car-buying experts recommend avoiding dealerships that charge reconditioning fees altogether. But remember that the out-the-door price is what matters at the end of the day, so it’s worth comparing prices at multiple dealerships to find the best deal.

Reddit is an online forum where consumers share their thoughts in “threads” on various topics. The popular site includes plenty of discussion on financial subjects like car buying, so we sifted through Reddit threads to get a sense of how users feel about reconditioning fees. People post anonymously, so we cannot confirm their individual experiences or circumstances.

Industry observers note that reddit consumers are generally skeptical toward reconditioning fees. Many users view these fees as a bait-and-switch tactic: dealers advertise an attractive price online and then tack on the fee at the dealership, inflating the actual out-the-door cost well above what was listed. Car buyers frequently share stories of being hit with reconditioning fees ranging from a few hundred dollars up to $2,000 or more, often with little or no evidence of what work was actually done.

It has been revealed that car-buying experts on Reddit point out that most dealerships already build reconditioning costs into the sticker price, so if the fee is listed separately, the dealership may be double-dipping. Several owners suggest that car buyers ask their dealer for an itemized breakdown of the work done, but most users recommend negotiating the total out-the-door price rather than individual fees.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that the last day to file a claim in Apple’s $250 million settlement over delayed Siri features is Dec.
  • Sources indicate that the class covers anyone in the US who bought an iPhone 15 Pro, iPhone 15 Pro Max or any iPhone 16 model between June 10, 2024, and March 29, 2025, the stretch when Apple was promoting a more personal Siri that hadn’t arrived yet.
  • Sources indicate that the iPhone 16 went on sale in September 2024 with Apple Intelligence at the center of its marketing.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that the last day to file a claim in Apple’s $250 million settlement over delayed Siri features is Dec. 21, and payouts could reach $95 per eligible iPhone.

Sources indicate that the class covers anyone in the US who bought an iPhone 15 Pro, iPhone 15 Pro Max or any iPhone 16 model between June 10, 2024, and March 29, 2025, the stretch when Apple was promoting a more personal Siri that hadn’t arrived yet. Filing takes a few minutes online, and each qualifying phone gets its own claim.

Sources indicate that the iPhone 16 went on sale in September 2024 with Apple Intelligence at the center of its marketing. However, the first AI features didn’t arrive until iOS 18.1, several weeks later, and the most heavily promoted one, a Siri that could pull personal context from your apps, was further delayed in March 2025.

Now you can turn that initial dismay into a payment in Apple’s $250 million legal settlement by signing up at a live website. The opt-in form is available only for a limited time, so get your name in the pool before it closes. Eligible buyers have until Dec. 21 to file, and each qualifying iPhone gets its own claim.

Apple settled a false advertising lawsuit brought by Clarkson Law Firm in May, agreeing to pay $250 million to customers who bought some iPhone models during a specified period. The lawsuit alleged that Apple misled customers by promising AI features that didn’t ship with the new devices. Apple denies all of the lawsuit’s allegations and denies that it did anything unlawful or improper.

If you purchased an iPhone 16 or iPhone 15 at launch, you may be entitled to receive a portion of the quarter-billion-dollar settlement. Payouts between $25 and $95 per eligible device are expected.

“Apple has reached a settlement to resolve claims related to the availability of two additional features. We resolved this matter to stay focused on doing what we do best, delivering the most innovative products and services to our users,” an Apple spokesperson mentioned in an earlier statement to CNET.

The court granted preliminary approval of the settlement on July 17. Then an Aug. 13 order moved up the final approval date by seven months.

“False advertising settlements aim to raise the floor of truth-telling, protect fair competition and increase consumer choice,” remarked Ryan Clarkson, co-lead counsel on the case and founder and managing partner of Clarkson Law Firm, in a statement to CNET. He claimed it’s the largest false-advertising settlement in history.

Apple lit up its flagship Fresh York City store to resemble Siri’s new color scheme.

Recent findings suggest that as of Sept. 21, you can go to SmartphoneAISettlement.com and enter your information to confirm your eligibility for monetary relief. People whom Apple and the settlement administrator determined would be eligible will also receive email or postal notices from the tech giant Verita directing them to the website.

In a recent development, the claims window closes on Dec. 21, 2026, so you have three months to act.

If you bought one of the following devices between June 10, 2024, and March 29, 2025, you could be eligible to receive a settlement payment:.

The iPhone 15 Pro and iPhone 15 Pro Max are included because they have the processor and memory to run Apple Intelligence features.

It’s estimated that approximately 36 million customers are eligible for this settlement.

Recent findings suggest that when Apple advertised its new iPhone 16 lineup in 2024, it emphasized how the models were optimized for AI features such as an enhanced Siri that could act as an intelligent agent. When the phones did arrive, Apple Intelligence wasn’t yet ready; its first features didn’t arrive until iOS 18.1, five weeks later.

According to the proposed settlement, “Apple allegedly saturated the market with deceptive ads, inducing consumers to purchase iPhones based on the promise of certain enhanced Siri features.”.

Industry observers note that some features of Apple Intelligence did ship soon after the introduction of the iPhone 16 and iOS 18, including Visual Intelligence, Live Translation, Writing Tools, Genmoji and Clean Up. But those weren’t the advanced features Apple highlighted. In fact, the type of intelligent interactions Apple advertised is only starting to show up in Siri AI, which is part of iOS 27, which was released in early September.

Recent findings suggest that according to the settlement, Apple needed to provide the information about affected customers within five days of the settlement approval. As of late July, preliminary approval has been granted by the court.

After the data is provided and verified, a 45-day notice period begins to inform potential consumers that they’re eligible for a payment.

It has been revealed that on Aug. 13, US District Court Judge Noël Wise granted approval to push forward the date from Sept. 29, 2027, to Feb. 24, 2027.

Provided approval is granted, the first checks or deposits will arrive sometime within a 60-day window after February next year, depending on court dates and possible extensions.

The Winter Solstice Is Coming: A Guide to the Longest Night

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (810 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • This was taken with the main camera as a ProRaw photo.
  • Thanksgiving is almost here, as is Cyber Monday, but soon it’ll be officially winter.
  • The winter solstice has a few different meanings, so here are all of them.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This was taken with the main camera as a ProRaw photo. Notice the lights on the tree, compared to the green hue of the street lighting and blue and pink tones in the sky.

Thanksgiving is almost here, as is Cyber Monday, but soon it’ll be officially winter. The winter solstice is on Dec. 21, when we’ll experience Earth’s shortest, darkest day.

The winter solstice has a few different meanings, so here are all of them. The most common definition, and the one you’re most likely familiar with, is that it denotes the shortest day and longest night of the year on Earth. These times vary depending on your location on the globe, but the further north you live, the less sunlight you’ll get. In the tropics, they’ll get about 12 hours of sunlight. In Sweden, it’ll be closer to 6 hours. In Svalbard, there isn’t any.

In a recent development, the reason this occurs is due to the second definition of the winter solstice: During this time, the North Pole is tilted as far away from the sun as it can get. According to The Farmer’s Almanac, the moment at which the Earth’s axis is physically tilted as much as it can be is at 3:50 p.m. ET on Monday, Dec. 21. After that moment, the process will begin to reverse until the South Pole takes its turn during the summer solstice. At that point, the North Pole will be at its closest tilt to the sun, giving us the longest day and shortest night of the year for the Northern Hemisphere.

Recent findings suggest that sunset will occur at its earliest time on Dec. 21.

It’ll vary by location. The southern US will have the most sunlight, with Florida getting a little over 10 hours during the winter solstice. The Midwest and Great Lakes portion of the country will get roughly nine hours. The Pacific Northwest can expect a little less than nine hours. Southern Alaska will get about six hours, and the northern areas of Alaska will see around three hours.

According to recent reports, if you want to see how your area will fare, Time and Date has a sunrise and sunset tool you can use. Input your zip code into the search bar, and you’ll be able to see your sunrise and sunset times.

Industry observers note that the city of Utqiaġvik, Alaska, will have it worse than most in the US: It won’t get any sun at all. The sun won’t rise there again until late January. We hope the people living there packed their vitamin D supplements.

The autumn equinox was just a couple of months ago, so you may be curious about the differences. A solstice occurs when the Earth’s poles are tilted as far away from the sun as they’ll be over the course of one year, which is also one orbit around the sun. The equinoxes take place at the halfway points between each solstice. The autumn equinox takes place in September between the summer and winter solstices, while the spring equinox takes place in March between the winter and summer.

During an equinox, the poles are minimally tilted, and the days are as even as they can be. This also has a couple of other interesting side effects: The sun is pointed directly at the equator during an equinox, and the sun will rise and set directly east and west, respectively.

Recent findings suggest that humans use the solstices and equinoxes to mark the change of the seasons. There are two equinoxes and two solstices, which mark the start and end dates for Earth’s four seasons.

Decorating with evergreen trees, like with a wreath, is what they used to do to celebrate the winter solstice.

In a recent development, while the solstice is close to the holidays, celebrations for the winter solstice have been around for significantly longer, and some winter solstice traditions have become Christmas traditions as well. One of the most historically famous winter solstice celebrations is Yule, a winter festival originating thousands of years ago among the ancient Norse. It became commonly celebrated in Europe and involved bonfires and massive feasts. Yule celebrations also included decorating with evergreen tree decorations, like holly and ivy.

If these sound familiar, it’s because Christmas co-opted many of those traditions centuries ago, and the two traditions have kind of merged into a single seasonal holiday. The terms Yule and Christmas are often used interchangeably these days in many cultures.

According to recent reports, so if you want to celebrate the winter solstice, just do all of the stuff you would normally do for the holidays. Burn a Yule log, decorate a tree, eat a substantial feast with your family and hang up mistletoe and wreaths — those are all hat tips to traditional winter solstice celebrations.

Last night's Full Moon may be behind us, but the Moon is still massive and bright in the sky. It's now entered its Waning Gibbous phase, although it will still look almost identical to yesterday, with only a tiny sliver of its illuminated surface beginning to wane.

As of Wednesday, Nov. 25, the NASA's Daily Moon Guide tracker tells us the Moon is in the Waning Gibbous phase, with 99% of its surface visible.

If you don't have any visual aids, you can still see the Mares Serenitatis and Crisium, as well as the Copernicus Crater. With binoculars, you'll also see the Mare Nectaris, the Endymion Crater, and the Mare Humorum. And if you have a telescope, you'll get to see all this plus the Apollo 16 and 17 landing spots, plus the Rima Hyginus.

In a recent development, in North America, the next Full Moon will take place on December 23. In other time zones it will fall on December 24.

Industry observers note that it takes around 29.5 days for the Moon to move through all its phases, according to NASA. Throughout this period, the Moon's position relative to Earth and the Sun determines how much of its illuminated surface we can see. Starting with a Fresh Moon, the visible portion gradually increases until it reaches a Full Moon, before shrinking again as the cycle comes back around.

New Moon - The Moon is between Earth and the sun, so the side we see is dark (in other words, it's invisible to the eye).

Waxing Crescent - A small sliver of light appears on the right side (Northern Hemisphere).

It has been revealed that first Quarter - Half of the Moon is lit on the right side. It looks like a half-Moon.

Waxing Gibbous - More than half is lit up, but it's not quite full yet.

Full Moon - The whole face of the Moon is illuminated and fully visible.

It has been revealed that waning Gibbous - The Moon starts losing light on the right side. (Northern Hemisphere).

Third Quarter (or Last Quarter) - Another half-Moon, but now the left side is lit.

Waning Crescent - A thin sliver of light remains on the left side before going dark again.

Tech Report: What Are Repositioning Cruises?

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1052 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nerdwallet

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that A repositioning cruise is a one-way sailing that moves a ship from one region to another.
  • Repositioning cruises are most common in spring (roughly March to May) and fall (roughly September to November), though they can occur at other times of year.
  • Because ships are crossing oceans, these trips often include many days at sea.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that A repositioning cruise is a one-way sailing that moves a ship from one region to another. For example, many ships sail in the Mediterranean Sea during the summer and move to the Caribbean Sea for the winter, and that trip between the two is a repositioning cruise.

Repositioning cruises are most common in spring (roughly March to May) and fall (roughly September to November), though they can occur at other times of year.

Because ships are crossing oceans, these trips often include many days at sea. For some travelers, that’s a chance to relax and enjoy the ship’s onboard amenities. Sometimes, these sailings can also be cheaper than traditional cruises.

Sources indicate that one key consideration for a repositioning cruise is that the embarkation and disembarkation ports will be different. This means you generally can’t buy a standard round-trip flight to and from the same city. Instead, you’ll need transportation to where the cruise starts and another way home from where it ends, which usually means two one-way flights (or one open-jaw ticket) unless you live near one of the ports. While these one-way sailings may be more affordable than traditional cruises, airfare costs may be higher.

This could be a great opportunity to redeem miles for your flight.

Another feature that sets these cruises apart is that stops along the way tend to include ports that aren’t traditionally part of regular itineraries. These might include islands like Bermuda, the Azores or the Canary Islands, and on some northern routes, Greenland.

Recent findings suggest that just keep in mind that the main purpose of these sailings is to get to a upcoming region for the next season’s itineraries rather than make daily port stops. So if you’re someone who wants to visit as many places as possible on a cruise, a repositioning sailing may not be the ideal choice.

Repositioning cruises are often longer than standard cruises, commonly running two to three weeks compared with about a week for a typical sailing, which may appeal to travelers looking for an extended vacation. The experience is often more relaxed, with many days at sea and less of a rush to book shore excursions or visit important sites when off the ship.

If there are particular ships with certain amenities — like tattoo parlors or massive waterparks — that you really want to experience, keep in mind that not all ships reposition between regions. Some stay in certain regions year-round.

It has been revealed that for ships that do change locations for the season, there are plenty of onboard activities to fill the time. You can enjoy shows, food and wine tastings, organized activities and time at the spa, pool or casino.

Many repositioning crossings are relatively smooth, and modern ships use stabilizers to reduce movement. But since these itineraries cross open ocean rather than staying closer to land, there can be more motion, especially on North Atlantic crossings in fall and winter.

If you tend to get seasick, this could be a dealbreaker. Even if a repositioning sailing is smooth, temperatures can be chilly on the open ocean, especially on northerly or spring and fall transatlantic routes, with strong winds that may make suntanning by the pool less appealing.

Sources indicate that you can book one of these sailings in the same way you would book a traditional cruise. But if you’re searching for dates and itineraries on a cruise line’s website, they may be listed as transatlantic, transpacific or Panama Canal sailings rather than repositioning cruises, though some lines do use the term "repositioning." There’s even a website that specializes in rounding up these cruises: RepoCruises.com.

It has been revealed that keep an eye out for themed sailings that focus on topics like wine, theater or music, where fellow guests on the ship may share similar interests. Cruise lines often schedule them on repositioning cruises to spur demand.

In a recent development, here are some repositioning cruises for 2027. They often take place during shoulder seasons, between the most popular cruising times in places like the Mediterranean or Caribbean.

Industry observers note that this journey repositions the ship from Miami, where it sails on Caribbean itineraries, to Seattle, where it will visit ports in Alaska during the spring and summer months. Departing April 8, 2027, the 18-night cruise includes stops at various ports in Colombia, Panama and Mexico, as well as San Diego and Los Angeles, before arriving in Seattle on April 26.

Regent Seven Seas Cruises' all-suite luxury ship Seven Seas Mariner will sail between Fresh York and Lisbon, making stops in Canada, Morocco and the Portuguese islands of Madeira and the Azores.

Departing April 29, 2027, the 16-night journey ends in Lisbon, Portugal, as the ship repositions to Europe, where it will sail various itineraries, including Mediterranean sailings later in the summer season.

Departing Seattle on Sept. 28, 2027, Norwegian Jade will sail to Yokohama, Japan, with stops in Alaska and northern Japan. This is a way to travel across the Pacific with less jet lag, since the journey takes place over several days, with ship clocks typically adjusted gradually (often an hour at a time) during the sailing. Note that the voyage also crosses the International Date Line.

Recent findings suggest that if Greenland has been on your bucket list, this 16-night sailing is a way to get up close and personal with its natural scenery. Departing Reykjavik on Aug. 25, 2027, Azamara Quest will sail from Iceland to the U.S. It will make stops in Greenland, Canada and Newly introduced England before reaching the Major Apple.

  • The FTC complaint alleges that Shein failed to follow through on its swift shipping policies, made it difficult for customers to resolve purchase complications and stifled negative customer reviews from seeing the light of day.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Shein, one of the biggest fast-fashion brands in the world, has been ordered to pay $100 million by the Federal Trade Commission, which alleges that the Singapore-based online retail giant engaged in deceptive practices that left millions of US customers dissatisfied with its products and policies.

The FTC complaint alleges that Shein failed to follow through on its swift shipping policies, made it difficult for customers to resolve purchase complications and stifled negative customer reviews from seeing the light of day.

The complaint also alleges problems with the tech giant’s supply chain, false information about the origin of the cotton used in its clothes, a failure to communicate shipping updates to customers and a lack of support for those whose packages were late or went missing altogether.

“The tech giant misled millions of consumers about its products, its suppliers and the authenticity of its customer reviews,” Christopher Mufarrige, director of the FTC’s Bureau of Consumer Protection, remarked in a statement on Tuesday.

Shein has ballooned over the past decade into the ultra-fast-fashion brand we know today, thanks in large part to the impact influencers have had on social media, posting videos trying on clothing supplied by the firm.

In 2026, the tech giant is estimated to ship roughly 1 million packages to US customers daily, according to the FTC. That number becomes even more astounding when you consider that Shein, the FTC alleges, employed just five customer service agents to answer calls from American customers.

This isn’t the first time Shein has faced negative scrutiny. Over the years, the company has faced allegations of numerous workers’ rights violations and is the largest polluter in the fast-fashion industry.

Sources indicate that according to Yale Climate Connections, the company emitted 16.7 million total metric tons of carbon dioxide into the atmosphere in 2023. Comparatively speaking, that’s more than the pollution output of four coal power plants. Shein has since pledged to improve its treatment of workers and reduce carbon emissions, but scrutiny persists.

Recent findings suggest that the $100 million will be used to compensate customers. And according to the FTC’s proposed order, the company, which earned roughly $50 billion in revenue in 2025, will not be able to continue advertising inaccurate shipping and delivery times; negative reviews will no longer be hidden; and its customer service offering will be bolstered.

“The agreement does not constitute an admission of liability, and we continue to disagree with aspects of the FTC’s characterization of our business and compliance practices,” a Shein spokesperson told CNET.

Let's explore Anthropic's growth prospects, assess its competitive landscape, and examine what history suggests a $5,000 investment could be worth around the company's first-year IPO anniversary.

Including the full exercise of the underwriters' option to purchase additional shares, Anthropic's IPO generated $93.5 billion in gross proceeds. Anthropic also completed a concurrent $26 billion private placement involving Nvidia, Microsoft, Alphabet, Advanced Micro Devices, Broadcom, Micron Technology, and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing. Combined gross proceeds across the two transactions reached $119.5 billion.

According to recent reports, when Anthropic began trading, shares opened around $111.50. The company's valuation reached approximately $2 trillion, instantly propelling Anthropic to one of the world's most valuable companies. Shares subsequently climbed to $115.10, although investors have since grown more cautious about the company over the last week.

It has been revealed that anthropic's revenue growth is nothing short of extraordinary. In 2023, the company generated just $41 million in sales. By 2025, the company's top-line had increased by more than 100x -- reaching $4.6 billion.

According to recent reports, during the third quarter alone, Anthropic grew revenue by approximately 1,127% year over year to $17 billion. Furthermore, the manufacturer exited October with an annualized revenue run rate of $81 billion.

Despite Claude's historic adoption rate, Anthropic's infrastructure requirements and competitive landscape complicate the firm's investment thesis.

NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

Industry observers note that anthropic faces competition from two categories. The first stems from other dedicated frontier AI developers such as OpenAI, the maker of ChatGPT. The second source of competition includes diversified technology companies such as Alphabet and SpaceX, which develop Gemini and Grok, respectively.

It has been revealed that big tech conglomerates have alternative revenue streams that can help finance their AI ambitions. Alphabet operates high-margin advertising and cloud computing businesses, while SpaceX generates revenue from satellite connectivity and rocket rolls out.

In a recent development, these financial resources afford Anthropic's rivals greater flexibility when pricing their AI products. As large language models (LLMs) become increasingly sophisticated and open-weight alternatives mature, Anthropic may face pressure to reduce prices in order to retain customers.

According to recent reports, meanwhile, Anthropic has accumulated $901 billion in infrastructure commitments stretching across the next several years. During the third quarter alone, the firm incurred $9.9 billion in computing and infrastructure expenses.

Sources indicate that if rising competition drives AI pricing lower while capacity expenses remain elevated, Anthropic could struggle to translate its revenue growth into sustainable profits. This outcome could cause investors to re-rate the company with a lower price-to-sales (P/S) multiple, even as its revenue continues expanding.

To understand how Anthropic stock might perform over the next year, let's consider how several major technology IPOs performed during their first year as public companies.

According to recent reports, amazon and Alphabet generated first-year returns of 281% and 179%, respectively, while Tesla stock appreciated by 18%. By contrast, Meta Platforms, Uber, and Rivian experienced first-year declines of 31%, 21%, and 67%, respectively.

In a recent development, although the average first-year return across these six companies washed out to about 60%, the results were heavily skewed by Amazon and Alphabet. The median return was actually negative, while the average and median maximum drawdowns during the first year were approximately 49% and 46%, respectively.

Perhaps more relevant to Anthropic is a separate analysis of the 10 largest U.S. IPOs between 2000 and 2024. Across this cohort, the average first-year return was -26%, while the median return was -34%. Furthermore, the average and median maximum drawdowns were 54% and 53%, respectively.

In a recent development, using Anthropic's recent share price of $80, a decline consistent with the average or median first-year return among these mega-IPOs would imply a stock price between $53 and $59. Under these scenarios, a $5,000 investment would shrink to roughly $3,300 and $3,700.

Recent findings suggest that conversely, if Anthropic were to match the average first-year return of Alphabet or Amazon, shares could reach $223. This would transform a $5,000 investment into nearly $14,000.

Industry observers note that ultimately, history illustrates just how unpredictable investing in IPO stocks can be. While the performance of previous mega-IPOs suggests Anthropic could trade lower around its first anniversary, the limited number of successful offerings demonstrates that meaningful upside is also possible.

Given the range of possible outcomes, investors considering buying Anthropic stock might be better served by gradually building a position over the long term as Claude’s competitive strengths and the company’s long-term profitability become clearer.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Keithen Drury – Nov 25, 2026 at 5:23PM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Advanced Micro Devices ›.

According to recent reports, AMD (AMD -1.75%) has been a fantastic stock to own in 2026. The stock has risen around 100% so far, though it was up 200% at the start of October. AMD became a popular choice for many investors, including the smart money in hedge funds. However, now that the latest round of 13-F filings has come out, it's clear that selling AMD has become a trend among fund managers.

Two major funds sold all of their shares during the third quarter: Appaloosa Management, run by David Tepper, and Coatue Management, run by Philippe Laffont. When giant funds like this sell, it's normally time to start thinking about selling your shares as well. So, is it time to move on from AMD stock?

Sources indicate that first, let's tackle the business. AMD has always played second fiddle to Nvidia (NVDA -3.91%) in the data center industry, as Nvidia's hardware and software have always been a step ahead of AMD's. However, AMD's products are becoming more popular among certain customers because they are cheaper. While they may not be as capable, power-efficient, or user-friendly, they can be quite useful if they’re not being tasked with a wide variety of operations.

NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

In a recent development, this has led to more adoption of AMD's products, and AMD's Q3 results back that up. The company experienced 97% year-over-year revenue growth in its data center division to $8.5 billion during Q3. However, AMD is more than just a data center company. Its overall growth rate was 45% year-over-year to $11.5 billion, as its client and gaming segment decreased year-over-year, partially offset by increasing Embedded processors doing well. Overall, those are solid results for AMD, but there's just one problem: It's far smaller than Nvidia.

Sources indicate that AMD already has a tough enough time being compared to Nvidia's products. For it to be a better investment than Nvidia, it should be showing stronger growth, but it's not. During its fiscal third quarter (ended in October), Nvidia's overall revenue rose 103% year over year to nearly $116 billion. So, Nvidia is 10 times larger than AMD. On the data center side, Nvidia's revenue rose 110% to $108 billion.

Nvidia has the technology edge and the growth edge. However, AMD has dramatically outperformed Nvidia this year, and there is one obvious reason for that: valuation.

AMD PE Ratio (Forward) data by YCharts.

In a recent development, sometimes, a stock goes up not because the business is doing well, but because the market is willing to pay more for the stock. That's exactly what's going on here, and it has gotten a bit out of control with AMD's stock.

AMD is one of the pricier stocks on the market, trading at 81 times trailing earnings and 21 times next year’s earnings.

Because 13F filings don't reveal exact transaction dates, we don't know whether these funds exited early in Q3 or right before the quarter ended—when AMD traded at over 80 times forward earnings and nearly 40 times next year's earnings—though either way they missed the stock's early-October peak.

Still, when you compare price tags, AMD is far more expensive, because Nvidia trades at 15 times trailing earnings and 8.6 times next year's earnings. Nvidia is clearly the far better value, and with it growing faster at a much larger scale, Nvidia’s stock looks like a far better investment.

According to recent reports, so, while now may not be the best time to sell AMD compared to a month and a half ago, I still think investors would be wise to move on to another AI stock. Many artificial intelligence investments are on huge sale right now, but AMD is not one of them.

Another day, another substantial swing. This one's lower, but don't count on it starting a trend: We keep seeing mortgage rates move back and forth, but no one's expecting rates to take a dive. If you're watching this space because you're waiting to refinance, it's unlikely your wait is about to end.

The average interest rate on a 30-year, fixed-rate mortgage dropped to 7.13% APR, according to rates provided to NerdWallet by Zillow. This is 25 basis points lower than yesterday and unchanged from a week ago. (A basis point is one one-hundredth of a percentage point.).

It has been revealed that the amount of day-to-day discrepancy we've been seeing prompted me to take a little cruise around the web this morning to see what 30-year rates lenders are advertising. Mortgage lenders' rates are never identical, but when we're seeing rapid change, the gaps between lenders tend to widen — and that's for sure what I saw. I looked at six different lenders, and saw a nearly 70-basis-point difference between the highest and lowest APRs. (And yes, that was looking for the same loan amount, location and so on.).

Recent findings suggest that my point is, whether you're looking to buy or refinance, make sure to shop multiple lenders. You're the same candidate bringing the same financials to each one, but you could end up with extremely different rate quotes. And it pays to compare. Freddie Mac estimates that comparing at least two lenders could save you up to $600 per year in interest. Compare four or more, and that savings is over $1,200 annually.

Sources indicate that here are the average APRs we're seeing today, as well as movement over the past month for context. For more, keep reading below the charts.

» Take the next step: Compare mortgage rates from NerdWallet’s top lenders.

Mortgage rates are constantly changing, since a major part of how rates are set depends on reactions to new inflation reports, job numbers, Fed meetings, global news ... you name it. For example, even tiny changes in the bond market can shift mortgage pricing.

Sources indicate that mortgage rates may be lower today, but like I mentioned above, it's been more of a seesaw than a ski slope — and we may be about to hit the high side again. The latest Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index is due out tomorrow morning. Recently, when rates have moved higher, inflation's been in the mix.

Strong inflation's generally bad for borrowing, including to buy a home, because higher interest rates are the remedy. Raising the federal funds rate (the short-term borrowing rate the central bankers of the Federal Reserve actually set) is the Fed's main tactic for managing inflation. While the Fed doesn't set mortgage rates, its decisions influence the entire economy. That includes mortgage lenders, who tend to adjust rates ahead of its decisions.

We already know how PCE's likely to go, since it's the last of the three big inflation measures to be released. We've already gotten last month's Consumer Price Index and Producer Price Index. October's CPI came in worse than predicted, showing widespread price increases. (When most of the increase is driven by one area, it's easier to be optimistic that inflation can be contained.) And October’s PPI showed wholesale inflation climbed at its fastest pace in almost four years. PPI measures the price businesses pay for things, so it's often a preview of what consumers could face once those costs get passed along.

It has been revealed that predictions for October PCE aren't great, so at this point the hope is that the numbers aren't even worse than expected. And again, PCE's out tomorrow morning. We'll know whether we're getting seconds (actually, thirds) of bad October inflation news well before the turkey hits the table on Thursday.

Markets are right now anticipating a quarter-point hike at the Fed's December meeting. Even though that'll remain the most likely outcome, a poor showing from PCE could spark speculation about a half-point hike. That probably won't be good for mortgage rates.

But back to the upcoming holiday: Markets will be closed on Thanksgiving, and Black Friday's a half day, so we'll all have a bit of a break this week. Mortgage rates don't move much when the markets aren't moving. I won't be here to talk to you about mortgage rates, either, 'cause NerdWallet gives us Thursday and Friday off. Happy Thanksgiving!

Also consider your goals: Are you trying to lower your monthly payment, shorten your loan term or turn home equity into cash? For example, you might be more comfortable with paying a higher rate for a cash-out refinance than you would for a rate-and-term refinance, so long as the overall costs are lower than if you kept your original mortgage and added a HELOC or home equity loan.

Connections can be played on both web browsers and mobile devices and require players to group four words that share something in common.

Each puzzle features 16 words and each grouping of words is split into four categories. These sets could comprise of anything from book titles, software, country names, etc. Even though multiple words will seem like they fit together, there's only one correct answer.

It has been revealed that if a player gets all four words in a set correct, those words are removed from the board. Guess wrong and it counts as a mistake—players get up to four mistakes until the game ends.

Players can also rearrange and shuffle the board to make spotting connections easier. Additionally, each group is color-coded with yellow being the easiest, followed by green, blue, and purple. Like Wordle, you can share the results with your friends on social media.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that grants are one of the best ways you can pay for your education.
  • In a recent development, grants can be used for tuition, course materials and other cost-of-attendance expenses.
  • Here’s how to use a college grant and what it can pay for.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that grants are one of the best ways you can pay for your education. It’s free money you aren’t expected to pay back.

In a recent development, grants can be used for tuition, course materials and other cost-of-attendance expenses. Some grants, depending on who awards them, require an application or have requirements you must meet before you can get your money.

Here’s how to use a college grant and what it can pay for.

There are four main types of grants:.

Federal grants come from the federal government.

State grants come from state programs and often can only be used at schools in that state.

Institutional grants come from your college or university, or even your program or major.

Private grants come from nonprofits, community organizations and individual donors.

To receive a federal grant, you must complete the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA). Most states require the FAFSA for state grants, and a few require a separate state application. You’ll need to complete the FAFSA for each year you’re enrolled in school. You may need to meet certain eligibility requirements, such as income limits, to get some grants. The FAFSA is how you apply for the Pell Grant, which is a financial need-based grant. The FAFSA also determines eligibility for federal work-study, which is a job program rather than a grant.

Federal aid, including federal grants, typically requires students to meet satisfactory academic progress. This means you have to maintain a minimum grade point average and be on track to finish your degree on time, as determined by your school. Your school also sets how many credits you must take to qualify for grant funding.

Sources indicate that some grants — typically private or institutional grants — require an additional application that asks for transcripts, letters of recommendation and personal essays. Your school’s financial aid office or the grant provider will have details on applying for specific grants.

In a recent development, after you submit the FAFSA, you’ll receive a financial aid award letter from each school you applied to, which outlines how much in federal, state and institutional grants you’ve been offered. You must accept your aid to receive it.

According to recent reports, most grants will be disbursed directly to your college or university. Your school will apply the grant money first to tuition, fees and any other charges it bills, such as housing or a meal proposal.

In some cases, you may receive more grant money than your school bills, which is the best-case scenario. If that happens to you, any leftover funds will likely be refunded to you. Refund timelines vary by school, so it may take some time to get your money. You can get your refund faster by setting up direct deposit with your school. You can then use the funds for other costs approved by your grant — some examples are detailed below.

If you have questions about your grant money, contact your college’s financial aid office.

In a recent development, grants can help cover cost-of-attendance expenses. Generally, you can use grant money to pay for tuition, textbooks, class materials, transportation, housing and food. Depending on your school’s policies, you can use grant money to cover summer classes or study abroad programs, too.

It has been revealed that some grants come with specific terms about how you can spend them. Check your financial aid award letter or, for a private or institutional grant, the school’s or organization’s website to find specifics.

Expenses grants aren’t meant for:.

Recent findings suggest that after your grant is applied to your tuition and school expenses, you can options to fill the gaps between what the grant covers and the total cost of your program. Some options include savings, scholarships, work-study, payment looks, federal student loans or, as a last resort, private loans. By using grants to pay for your college education, you may be able to borrow less.

To maximize the grants you’re eligible to receive, enter accurate information on the FAFSA and complete it as soon as you can — some funds are first-come, first-served. Also, don’t limit yourself to federal or state grants — search and apply for as many privately funded grants as you can find.

Recent findings suggest that your grant money usually goes straight to your college or university to pay your tuition and fees. Anything that is left over may be disbursed to you for other school-related costs.

In a recent development, yes, but it depends on your grant. Housing is part of your cost of attendance, so you can use grant money to pay for off-campus rent.

You don’t have to pay back a grant as long as you continue to meet all requirements for the grant, such as staying enrolled. You can use grant money on school and school-related expenses. Some grants may require you to meet eligibility requirements such as a minimum GPA or state residency. If you receive more grant money than your cost of attendance for a given school term, ask your financial aid office if you can put that grant money toward next year’s cost of attendance.

If you have a federal grant like a Pell Grant, these are examples when you may have to repay all or part of the grant:.

You withdrew from your program.

You received enough scholarship money to reduce your federal aid need.

Recent findings suggest that it depends. You can usually use grant money to buy a laptop. Computers are considered course materials, which fall under cost-of-attendance expenses, so they can be covered by a grant. However, always double-check with the grant provider and your financial aid award letter to ensure that you’re following all restrictions. Whether you can use grant money to cover a laptop depends on your school’s policies and how much grant money you receive.

Recent findings suggest that if you get more grant money than your school bills you, you’ll likely receive the leftover money to spend on other cost-of-attendance expenses. You can use this money on living costs such as transportation or housing. Grant money often goes mostly toward tuition, so a refund isn’t guaranteed.

In a recent development, grant and scholarship money is generally tax-free when you use it for tuition, required fees, books and required class supplies. If you have additional questions, consider talking to a tax professional.

At about $42.57 as of Wednesday's market close, the stock is down roughly 70% from its 52-week high of $138.25 and down nearly 77% from its all-time closing high.

Wall Street analysts, meanwhile, are lowering their expectations, but not by much, and the gap between the bulls and the market is the crux of the debate.

Cantor Fitzgerald on Wednesday lowered its price target to $96 from $100 and kept its overweight rating. The firm stated fears about CoreWeave's business model "continue to be overblown" and told clients to "be thankful for the discount the market has given them." Cantor said the cut reflects a higher expected share count, because raising equity at a lower stock price means issuing more shares.

A day earlier, Evercore ISI cut its target to $80 from $100 and kept its outperform rating. The analyst said the sharp correction in AI stocks has put more focus on pricing and downside risks, and assessed where the sell-off "might have overextended.".

From Wednesday's closing price, Cantor's target implies upside of about 125%, and Evercore's implies about 89%.

According to recent reports, coreWeave's lenders are far less relaxed. Its notes due October 2031 fell nearly 2 cents to about 74 cents on the dollar on Wednesday, pushing their yield to 17.91%, Reuters reported, citing Tradeweb data. Its notes due June 2030 fell to a record low of 76.55 cents. The cost of insuring CoreWeave's debt against default has also climbed to levels usually seen at distressed companies.

According to recent reports, A yield near 18% is a warning sign. It means lenders are demanding a return closer to what you'd expect from a stock, and bondholders get paid before shareholders. CoreWeave does have a cheaper way to borrow: its banks are preparing to sell a $4.5 billion loan backed by chips it is installing for Meta Platforms (META +3.40%) as soon as next week, Bloomberg reported. Because Meta is the customer, that loan is expected to be rated investment-grade and priced around 7% to 7.5%. But that kind of financing only works for capacity tied to a specific customer contract, not for the company as a whole.

Even Cantor concedes the market is "extremely focused" on one concern: CoreWeave's need for as much as $5 billion of "parent capital" in 2027, meaning money raised at the manufacturer level to support its build-out. Cantor thinks management should address the funding plan "sooner rather than later" and remarked a clear answer could act as a "potential clearing event" for the stock.

That's the crux. If CoreWeave raises capital through newly introduced shares at today's prices, existing shareholders are diluted. If it borrows, it pays rates the bond market has just pushed sharply higher. Either route makes it harder to reach the upside in those price targets.

For most investors, not yet. The analysts may well be right that the sell-off overshot, and Cantor says its review of how CoreWeave resigns customer contracts gives it more confidence in the model. But when the firm's own bonds yield nearly 18%, the market is pricing in real risk that shareholders would absorb first.

Recent findings suggest that risk-tolerant investors who believe in long-term AI demand could start a small position, but the smarter move is to wait for the 2027 funding strategy Cantor is asking for. If management lays out a credible way to raise that money without heavy dilution, the stock could rerate rapidly. Until then, there are less leveraged ways to own the AI build-out among cloud stocks and semiconductor stocks.
