📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

An injury-time penalty from returning hero Raul Jimenez ensured Wolves came away with a point in their Championship opener after Blackburn had produced a comeback.

Wolves led through Marshall Munetsi’s cool finish on 18 minutes only for Sean McLoughlin’s first Blackburn goal to draw the visitors level on 27 minutes with a well-timed run and header.

According to recent reports, the visitors turned the game around on 48 minutes through Andri Gudjohnsen’s close-range strike only for substitute Jimenez to level the game three minutes into injury time from the spot after Ryan Alebiosu handled the ball in the box. Jimenez and his wife marked his return to Molineux by giving 5,000 fans black scarves emblazoned with the words ‘Si Senor’ - a nod to his song - and Jimenez did not disappoint as he rifled in his penalty.

Sources indicate that LATE DRAMA! 😱Raul Jimenez cooly converts from the penalty spot, deep into added time to save a point for Wolves 🔥 pic.twitter.com/5h2lMxcHNU.

Cesar Peixoto wants Wolves to play with their heads rather than their hearts after the home side rescued a late point in the first game of the Championship season following relegation. Wolves replaced Rob Edwards with Portuguese coach Peixoto during the summer and he felt his side’s loss of organisation allowed Blackburn to take control of the game.

Sources indicate that peixoto said: “One point is not what we want, we want three points. We lost some organisation in the second half and played more with our hearts and not our heads and brains.

“We have to keep our mental stability during the 90 minutes because we’re better when we’re organised. We need to play our way with our identity. It’s a lesson for us to understand when we lose organisation it’s more difficult for us and more easy for the opposition.

Sources indicate that “We’re working hard to bring more solutions [into the club] but we need to work hard with the players we have. It’s the first game, there’s a lot to work on and a lot to improve.”.

It has been revealed that tony Mowbray took charge of Blackburn in the league for the first time since returning to the club for a second stint in the dugout. Rovers recorded their lowest league finish since Mowbray’s first stint in charge of the club last term but the Blackburn boss is confident his side have enough to beat the drop and climb up the table this campaign.

Industry observers note that mowbray said: “Ultimately, it feels like a defeat, it’s a bit disappointing and a bit frustrating. I just felt a lot of decisions were starting to swing their way. It’s harsh to take, I don’t think they deserved a second goal. We asked the players to be brave and we were collectively very strong.

“Everybody has us relegated, probably on the back of finishing 20th last season and losing a couple of our better players and not spending much money, which is a good motivation for the team. We deserved to win the game, we showed there’s enough quality to give teams problems and I hope there’s help on the way [in the transfer window].”.

The first chance of the season came the way of Blackburn as a cross-field pass found Alebiosu down the right, who floated a ball into the box only for an unmarked Oladipo Afolayan to head wide from eight-yards out.

However, Wolves scored the first goal of the latest campaign when Fer Lopez played a defence-splitting through ball into the path of Munetsi, who coolly found the net with a first time effort from the edge of the penalty area.

"A vibrant Molineux rejoices!" 🎉Marshall Munetsi cooly slots home for Wolves to give them the lead on the opening night of the Championship season 🥶 pic.twitter.com/tVHdbNv3Hq.

Blackburn drew level through an unlikely source just nine minutes later as McLoughlin headed in his first-ever goal in English football in more than 150 games when he met Ryoya Morishita’s cross from the right at the near post.

The home side had chances to retake the lead before the break as Lopez curled a shot narrowly over the top from 20-yards while Kieran Trippier teed up Mateus Mane for a chance as the teenager found the top of the net from distance.

Blackburn turned the game on its head minutes after the break as Gudjohnsen turned home Afolayan’s deflected ball in from the right from close range to stun Molineux into silence.

"It's brilliantly worked by Blackburn Rovers!" 💥Andri Guðjohnsen finishes from close range to turn the game around and the visitors the lead 👏 pic.twitter.com/vkKQQezicK.

Peixoto introduced Jimenez from the bench on the hour mark but even the Mexican could not lift Wolves with Blackburn comfortable for long periods as frustration grew in the stands.

However, Alebiosu handled Jackson Tchatchoua’s cross from the left in injury time and the referee awarded a spot kick which allowed Jimenez to mark his Wolves return with an equaliser from 12-yards as he sent Balazs Toth the wrong way.

It has been revealed that “We see the ref’s position. The fact the ref makes the decision to give the penalty in my opinion, it is a bigger decision to give it then to not. We have got the luxury of the replays and we are still not sure. His whole body is outside the box.”.

When Wolverhampton Wanderers last attacked the Championship under a Portuguese manager newly introduced to English football, it proved a vintage season.

Molineux was under the spell of Nuno Espírito Santo in that 2017-18 campaign, and the big question is whether César Peixoto can lead a repeat nearly a decade later.

Peixoto was a surprise appointment in June, replacing Rob Edwards, and he has been entrusted with the mission of returning Wolves to the Premier League at the first time of asking.

“I have changed some things with set-pieces and some things in other moments of the game because I want the team to be organised and understand all the different moments within a match. During pre-season we have scored some goals from high pressing, but we will not be able to press high in every moment of every game. The players have to understand the game and recognise what each moment requires. It is crucial that we work as a team. When we can press high, we’ll press high. When we need to defend in a mid-block, we will stay organised. When the opposition pushes us deeper, which will sometimes happen, we have to be organised there as well.

Recent findings suggest that “There are a lot of crosses in the Championship, for example, so the team needs to understand what to do in those situations. Sources indicate that the 2026/27 Championship season kicks off at Molineux as Wolves host Blackburn, with the home side hoping to put the bad memories of last season firmly behind them. There are newly introduced playoff rules in place for this season, with six places now up for grabs in the play-offs.

Wolves are aiming to return to the Premier League at the first attempt, having endured a miserable season in the top flight last year as they finished bottom with just three wins to their name. It has been a summer of change at the club as they chose to change managers. Rob Edwards lost his job in what was a shock move and was replaced by 46-year-old Cesar Peixoto, with this being his first head coaching position outside of his home country Portugal. Back in 2017/18, Wolves won the Championship title led by Peixoto’s compatriot Nuno Espirito Santo.

“I am ready,” Peixoto told Wolves’ club website. “We have worked very hard during pre-season, and I think we have had a great pre-season. All the players have worked very, very hard and they understand what I want from them. I am ready and confident going into the first game. Football is football, whether it is in Portugal or England, but there are different characteristics to the game here. We have watched, observed and analysed the Championship. We did that work before I came to the club, so we know what to expect.

Sources indicate that “It is going to be a tough season with good teams, but we are prepared to fight for the three points game after game and week after week. We know what we want from the team and we know what our major goal is. We’re going to work very hard and fight to achieve that goal.”.

Sources indicate that they have brought in vast experience on the player side in the shape of Kieran Trippier and Raul Jimenez, who is back at Molineux three years after leaving for Fulham. Although they have lost Brazilian midfielder Joao Gomes to Aston Villa, most of their squad has stayed intact as they pursue promotion back to the top flight. It is a special year for the club as they celebrate their 150th anniversary.

Recent findings suggest that blackburn, led by experienced manager Tony Mowbray, did not enjoy a great season in the Championship last year, finishing down in 20th place and just five points above the relegation zone. 14 years have now passed since Blackburn last played in the top flight.

Sources indicate that “I think it is a tough start,” Mowbray noted. “On paper, I would suggest the first couple of games, particularly, jumped out as a tough start. One of the Premier League sides from last season, away from home. They have got a very talented squad, a pretty expensive squad. They have got some very good individual talent. Yet, there is an argument to say they have not won many football matches in the last calendar year. So, what we get, we will have to wait and see.”.

These sides last met in the FA Cup during the 2024/25 season, with Wolves winning that fourth-round tie 2-0 thanks to goals from Matheus Cunha and Gomes, both of whom are now plying their trade elsewhere. The omens would appear to be on Wolves’ side as they are unbeaten in their last eight league meetings with Blackburn. Both sides progressed to the second round of the League Cup last weekend, with Wolves beating Port Vale 3-0 and Blackburn overcoming Burton Albion 2-1.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Mortgage rates are a little lower this morning, and where they'll go next isn't totally clear.
  • The average interest rate on a 30-year, fixed-rate mortgage ticked down to 7.05% APR, according to rates provided to NerdWallet by Zillow.
  • In a recent development, inflation data out this morning looks, at first glance, like bad news for mortgage rates.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mortgage rates are a little lower this morning, and where they'll go next isn't totally clear.

The average interest rate on a 30-year, fixed-rate mortgage ticked down to 7.05% APR, according to rates provided to NerdWallet by Zillow. This is eight basis points lower than yesterday and 33 basis points lower than a week ago. (A basis point is one one-hundredth of a percentage point.).

In a recent development, inflation data out this morning looks, at first glance, like bad news for mortgage rates. But depending on how markets react, we could actually see lower mortgage rates. Keep reading after the charts for all the details.

Below are the average APRs we're seeing today, as well as movement over the past month for perspective.

According to recent reports, P.S. Markets will be closed tomorrow for Thanksgiving, and Black Friday's a half day, and mortgage rates don't move much when the markets aren't moving. I won't be here to talk to you about mortgage rates, either, 'cause NerdWallet gives us Thursday and Friday off. Happy Thanksgiving!

» Take the next step: Compare mortgage rates from NerdWallet’s top lenders.

Mortgage rates are constantly changing, since a major part of how rates are set depends on reactions to newly introduced inflation reports, job numbers, Fed meetings, global news ... you name it. For example, even tiny changes in the bond market can shift mortgage pricing.

In a recent development, like I mentioned above, it's not totally obvious where mortgage rates will head next. Let's walk through the two scenarios.

Recent findings suggest that here's why rates could go up: This morning, we got October's Personal Consumption Expenditures price index, also known as PCE. It's the last measure of inflation to come out each month, but it's also the Federal Reserve's preferred metric, so PCE gets a lot of attention.

The stats came in mostly as predicted, though it's not like the predictions were good — inflation's been overly strong for a while. But the core year-over-year figure, which came in a tenth of a percent over predictions, could prove troublesome. Core PCE removes categories that can be extra volatile, so it's considered a measure that reveals the underlying trend. In this case, the underlying trend is Not Good.

Recent findings suggest that it's already pretty much a lock that we'll see a rate hike at the Federal Reserve's December meeting, because yes, raising the federal funds rate is the Fed's main tool for taming inflation. The Fed doesn't set mortgage rates, but a rate-hiking cycle from the central bankers definitely keeps upward pressure on borrowing costs.

According to recent reports, on the other hand, here's why that same inflation data could help rates go down: Over the past several days, we've watched the stock market go on a wild ride, with the Anthropic IPO and the return of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. Yesterday, things weren't looking good for tech stocks, and these inflation numbers could make it even worse.

It has been revealed that the amount that tech companies have borrowed to fund AI buildout is a significant concern for investors, since companies will have to cover those costs before investors see any profits. It's already a substantial task, and if everything costs more thanks to inflation, it's that much harder.

This AI-related anxiety is rough on the stock market, but it's been a boon for Treasury bonds. More demand for bonds pushes up bond prices, which brings down bond yields (basically, the return investors get on a bond). Mortgage rates for 30-year loans are generally benchmarked to the yield on the 10-year Treasury note, so here's why you care about all of this: Lower Treasury yields means lower mortgage rates, too. If investors keep stressing about inflation eating into tech profits, we could see mortgage rates continue to move lower.

That was a lot of info on inflation, but inflation's not the only major metric influencing rates.

According to recent reports, let's back up for a second. The Federal Reserve tries to keep the economy steady by focusing on two key goals, often referred to as the Fed's dual mandate. One side is price stability — keeping inflation reasonable. The other is maximum employment, meaning those who want to work are able to find jobs.

Next week we'll shift our focus to the employment side of the Federal Reserve's mandate, because the first week of the month is always all about employment data. On Tuesday, Dec. 1, we'll kick things off with the Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey (JOLTS). JOLTS can tip us off to trends in the labor market; stuff like whether folks are leaving jobs voluntarily or if companies have openings that are going unfilled.

It has been revealed that on Wednesday, payroll firm ADP will release its monthly employment stats. ADP is looking at its own payroll data to get an idea of how the job market is growing or contracting. The numbers don't include the public sector, but ADP often provides a preview of how the jobs report will go.

The Employment Situation Summary, better known as the jobs report, drops on Friday. This is the major one, since it tells us the nation's unemployment rate. The jobs report's other major stat is, similar to ADP, how many jobs the economy added or lost in the previous month. Unlike ADP though, the jobs report is inclusive of everybody in the public and private sectors.

Lately the labor market's been looking super healthy, which is great news for the economy but less positive for mortgage rates. When hiring's strong, the Fed can feel safer raising the federal funds rate (that's the short-term borrowing rate the central bankers adjust). Higher rates tend to discourage businesses from borrowing and expanding, so if the job market's on shaky footing, the central bankers are going to be cautious about raising the benchmark rate.

Sources indicate that what we're seeing now though, where inflation is clearly the problem and employment's just fine, is a recipe for higher rates. Again, the Fed doesn't control mortgage rates, but the central bank being in rate-hike mode puts upward pressure on mortgage rates.

If we were to see employment falter in this latest round of numbers, it still probably wouldn't change the Fed's plan. That would be one poor month for the labor market versus months upon months of inflation running rampant — so yeah, they'll keep an eye on jobs, but inflation's still the scourge.

Our most likely source of lower mortgage rates in the short term is what I described above; investors who are leery of inflation and the promise of AI looking to the safe harbor of the bond market.

» Learn more: How the Fed affects mortgage rates.

Refinancing might make sense if today’s rates are at least 0.5 to 0.75 of a percentage point lower than your current rate (and if you proposal to stay in your home long enough to break even on closing costs).

With rates where they are right now, you could start considering a refi if your current rate is around 7.55% or higher — but there just aren't too many people for whom that's true.

Also consider your goals: Are you trying to lower your monthly payment, shorten your loan term or turn home equity into cash? For example, you might be more comfortable with paying a higher rate for a cash-out refinance than you would for a rate-and-term refinance, so long as the overall costs are lower than if you kept your original mortgage and added a HELOC or home equity loan.

If you're looking for a lower rate, use NerdWallet's refinance calculator to estimate savings and understand how long it would take to break even on the costs of refinancing.

There is no universal “right” time to start shopping — what matters is whether you can comfortably afford a mortgage now at today’s rates.

Industry observers note that if the answer is yes, don’t get too hung up on whether you could be missing out on lower rates later; you can refinance down the road. Focus on getting preapproved, comparing lender offers, and understanding what monthly payment works for your budget.

NerdWallet’s affordability calculator can help you estimate your potential monthly payment. If a upcoming home isn’t in the cards right now, there are still things you can do to strengthen your buyer profile. Take this time to pay down existing debts and build your down payment savings. Not only will this free up more cash flow for a future mortgage payment, it can also get you a better interest rate when you’re ready to buy.

Industry observers note that if you already have a quote you’re happy with, you should consider locking your mortgage rate, especially if your lender offers a float-down option. A float-down lets you take advantage of a better rate if the market drops during your lock period.

Rate locks protect you from increases while your loan is processed, and with the market forever bouncing around, that peace of mind can be worth it.

🤓 Nerdy Reminder: Rates can change daily, and even hourly. If you’re happy with the deal you have, it’s okay to commit.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, nvidia (NVDA -3.91%) has spent November at the center of a political storm, with Jensen Huang reinstated as CEO amid allegations that its chips were smuggled into China.
  • In a note published Wednesday, research firm TS Lombard said the Nvidia fallout has galvanized lawmakers, putting Congress on track to pass three to four latest chip export-control measures, most likely as part of the fiscal 2027 National Defense Authorization Act.
  • In a recent development, the bills would close several loopholes at once.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Jonathan Ponciano – Nov 25, 2026 at 5:58PM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Nvidia ›.

According to recent reports, nvidia (NVDA -3.91%) has spent November at the center of a political storm, with Jensen Huang reinstated as CEO amid allegations that its chips were smuggled into China. The stock fell another 4% on Wednesday. But the firm most at risk from Washington's response may be one most investors don't connect to the scandal at all.

In a note published Wednesday, research firm TS Lombard said the Nvidia fallout has galvanized lawmakers, putting Congress on track to pass three to four latest chip export-control measures, most likely as part of the fiscal 2027 National Defense Authorization Act. Grace Fan, the firm's managing director of global policy and disruptive themes research, said passage is a question of "when" and not "if," though a government shutdown fight around the Dec. 11 funding deadline could push it into early 2027.

In a recent development, the bills would close several loopholes at once. One would give Congress a say over exports of the most advanced AI chips. Another would require location tracking on exported AI chips to stop smuggling. A third would target Chinese companies renting U.S. chips through overseas cloud services. The centerpiece, the MATCH Act, goes after the machines that make chips rather than the chips themselves.

In a recent development, the MATCH Act would pressure U.S. allies, mainly the Netherlands and Japan, to match U.S. restrictions on the sale of chipmaking equipment to China. If they don't, TS Lombard said, the Senate version would direct the Commerce Department to impose the controls itself after about 150 days. The Senate bill also names every deep ultraviolet (DUV) lithography machine among the tools that couldn't go to China at all.

According to recent reports, that's why TS Lombard says the companies most at risk aren't U.S. equipment makers such as Applied Materials (AMAT -3.89%), Lam Research (LRCX -5.68%), and KLA (KLAC +0.41%), which already face U.S. rules. Instead, it points to ASML (ASML -2.47%), the Dutch lithography leader, and Japan's Tokyo Electron, along with several other Japanese suppliers. The Dutch government has said it opposes the bill.

Wednesday's trading didn't reflect that ranking. Lam fell 6% and Applied Materials 4%, while ASML dropped 2.5% to about $1,303, roughly 35% below its 52-week high.

In a recent development, there are two reasons ASML's exposure is shrinking. TS Lombard estimates that China will account for about 20% of ASML's sales this year, down from roughly 30% in fiscal 2025. Chinese chipmakers also front-loaded their purchases, building what the firm estimates is about three years' worth of DUV machines.

Industry observers note that that stockpile cuts both ways. It means fewer upcoming China orders were coming anyway, but it shifts the fight to servicing and spare parts, which the Senate version would also restrict. TS Lombard expects China to retaliate in measured ways, possibly by squeezing Dutch and Japanese companies, and sees a likely middle path in which some servicing licenses are traded for access to critical minerals.

According to recent reports, for long-term investors, yes, if you buy gradually. ASML is the only firm that makes the extreme ultraviolet (EUV) machines needed for the most advanced chips, and that position doesn't depend on China. A smaller China business is a hit to near-term sales, not to its long-term moat.

Sources indicate that the near-term risk is real, though. Headlines on the defense bill, the Dec. 11 funding deadline, and the Trump-Xi meeting at the G20 summit in Miami on Dec. 14-15 could all move the shares. Investors who want exposure to semiconductor stocks can use that volatility to build a position in stages rather than all at once, and keep an eye on Tokyo Electron and other tech stocks with heavy China exposure as the bill takes shape.

Ready for ‘The Great Lock In’? Viral Money Trend Can Improve Focus

💡 Key Takeaways
  • When it’s cold outside, it’s the ideal time to stay home, organize your finances, set some fresh money goals and make progress toward them.
  • That’s the promise of the viral winter money trend known as “The Great Lock In” that’s circulating on social media.
  • “You’re probably not doing too much,” claims Robert Baird, wealth manager at Cornerstone Financial Services in Southfield, Michigan.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When it’s cold outside, it’s the ideal time to stay home, organize your finances, set some fresh money goals and make progress toward them.

That’s the promise of the viral winter money trend known as “The Great Lock In” that’s circulating on social media.

“You’re probably not doing too much,” claims Robert Baird, wealth manager at Cornerstone Financial Services in Southfield, Michigan. “It gets dark early. So those can be great months to lock into saving and not spend in excess.”.

One important component of the Great Lock In is developing upcoming routines that will last well into 2027, indicates Jordan Mangaliman, founder and fiduciary wealth advisor at GoldLine Wealth Management in Fullerton, California.

“We want a long-term habit versus a Band-Aid fix,” he indicates. “In today’s economy, money goes in and out so blindingly fast.”.

Ready to join the movement? Here’s how to get started.

In a recent development, what’s your money moonshot? Maybe it’s paying off all your credit card debt or purchasing a home. Or spending less than you earn. Defining it is the first step toward achieving it.

In a recent development, “Spend a lot of time identifying what that goal is,” Baird indicates. “Everyone’s in a different position, so comparing yourself to what you see online might not be applicable.”.

Even while setting ambitious money goals, it’s worth grounding them in reality, Mangaliman says.

If you want to save a larger portion of your income, he suggests trying the newly introduced saving pattern for a couple of months to see how it feels rather than saying you’ll do it forever and then getting frustrated.

“It’s a marathon, not a sprint,” Mangaliman adds.

Once you’ve outlined those substantial goals for your Great Lock In, create a budget to help you achieve them, Baird says.

According to recent reports, he suggests combing through your previous credit or debit card spending to see where your money is going. Then you can decide what you want to change or shift. Using a tool like the 50/30/20 budget calculator can also help. This approach allots 50% of take-home pay toward needs, 30% toward wants and 20% toward savings and debt payments beyond the minimum.

It has been revealed that baird suggests including saving as a line item in your budget so you don’t forget to do it. “Building that cost into your budget will put you in a better position later,” he says.

Any Great Lock In should include growing your savings, because that makes achieving other goals easier, Baird indicates.

In a recent development, “Maybe there’s something you could cut in the short term to build up that savings,” he states. Good targets include subscription services, food delivery, entertainment and travel costs.

Saving more is especially challenging in today’s environment, when everyday expenses like gas are higher than they were a year ago.

Baird indicates that makes winter a good time to try to reduce costs. There can be fewer temptations to go out and spend money when the days are shorter and the temperatures are colder.

Sources indicate that mangaliman recommends setting aside three to six months’ worth of expenses, although even a smaller amount is helpful. “Ultimately it’s about what you can afford,” he states. “It’s the foundation of your financial house.”.

Along with building savings, paying down high-interest debt is another pillar of the Great Lock In.

With credit card interest rates higher than they were a few years ago, carrying credit card debt has gotten more expensive. “I would consider applying some savings to paying down debt, especially right now when your debt is costing you more than you can earn in savings,” Baird indicates. (You still want to reserve an emergency fund to cover unexpected expenses.).

Industry observers note that “High-interest debt is one of the biggest thieves of wealth,” Mangaliman notes. And one way to avoid turning to debt again in the future is to build up that emergency fund so it’s there for you if you need it.

Recent findings suggest that even when you are committed to a Great Lock In, some hiccups along the way are inevitable. Success depends on continuing anyway.

Sources indicate that “It’s like a diet,” Baird indicates. “Just because you ate ice cream on a Sunday doesn’t mean on Monday you can’t go right back to being disciplined again.”.

“Be kind to yourself and do everything in moderation,” Mangaliman suggests. Just wanting to improve your finances is already a great first step, he states.

Sources indicate that in fact, he embraces the Great Lock In mentality himself. “There’s an old saying: It’s not how you start, but how you finish,” he says. “And you want to finish the year on a strong note so you carry those habits into 2027 and beyond.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Jonathan Ponciano – Nov 25, 2026 at 6:00PM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Palantir Technologies ›.

It has been revealed that michael Burry made his name betting against the housing market before the 2008 financial crisis. This week, with tech stocks in a steep slide, he did something somewhat unusual for him: He stopped betting against the market.

In a post on his Substack, Cassandra Unchained, Burry remarked he had sold the rest of his put options on the Nasdaq-100, bearish bets that pay off when the index falls. "Globally, my portfolio is more long, and less short, than it has been in some time," he wrote. Apart from puts on Palantir Technologies (PLTR +1.50%) and MetLife (MET +0.57%), he added, "I am temporarily almost entirely long.".

According to recent reports, michael Burry. Image source: Getty Images.

Industry observers note that burry is turning more bullish after a sharp drop. The Nasdaq Composite closed Tuesday at 23,733.54, down 14.5% from its Oct. 6 close, and the Nasdaq-100 fell 16% over the same stretch. The Composite is down about 7% in November alone, as doubts about whether the AI spending boom will pay off, newly introduced tariff proposals, and the turmoil around Nvidia's leadership have weighed on AI stocks.

It has been revealed that puts gain value as an index falls, so selling them after a slide is a way to lock in profits. Burry said much of his cash, about 25% of the portfolio, came from profitable put options plus money added to the account.

It has been revealed that the most key word in his post may be "temporarily." Burry mentioned he is "continuing to assess short opportunities," and he hasn't said the market has bottomed. He also kept his Palantir puts, even though Palantir shares, at about $164 on Wednesday, already sit roughly 23% below their 52-week high.

Burry disclosed large put positions on Nvidia and Palantir in late 2025 after warning about an AI bubble. Shifting from that stance to mostly long tells you he thinks a good part of the downside he expected has now played out, at least for the broad index.

For most investors, the answer is not to copy his trades. Burry can reverse a position in a day and write about it afterward, so by the time a move becomes news, he may have changed it again. Short-selling and options are tools most individual investors shouldn't rely on.

The useful lesson is in how he's behaving. He took profits on a bet that worked, he's holding a massive cash cushion, and he's staying selective about what he owns. You can do a version of that: Make a list of quality tech stocks you'd be glad to own for five years, and buy them in stages if the sell-off continues, rather than all at once. Keep enough cash on the side that you're never forced to sell in a downturn.

Industry observers note that markets are closed Thursday for Thanksgiving and close early on Friday, so expect thin trading and bigger swings to end the week. If Burry's right that the worst of the Nasdaq's slide is behind it, patient buyers will be rewarded. If he's wrong, he's already told you he can switch back, and investors buying in stages will have room to do the same.

Cross-Functional Collaboration Is Fashion’s New Competitive Advantage

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Maximilien Abadie, Deputy CEO and a member of the Executive Committee, Lectra.
  • Industry observers note that ​Speed and creativity have always been defining features of the fashion industry.
  • Companies that create the digital and cultural infrastructure to support cross-functional collaboration make it possible to unify workflows, anticipate challenges earlier and share data for faster, better decisions.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Maximilien Abadie, Deputy CEO and a member of the Executive Committee, Lectra.

Industry observers note that ​Speed and creativity have always been defining features of the fashion industry. In a climate marked by fragmentation and continuing volatility, accelerating time to market and achieving the all-important five R’s (right place, right product, right price, right quantities and right consumer) have become less about moving faster at individual stages and more about improving how information is shared and decisions are made across the value chain.

Companies that create the digital and cultural infrastructure to support cross-functional collaboration make it possible to unify workflows, anticipate challenges earlier and share data for faster, better decisions. This transforms the way a tech giant creates, manufactures and sells their products. ​.

Every product that makes it to market is shaped by contributions from hundreds of different individuals, many of whom do not speak the same language or share a common perspective. The linear, step-by-step approach to collection development—design followed by development, then production and ending with marketing, merchandising and e-commerce—struggles to provide the agility needed to respond quickly to the dynamism that characterizes this industry.

When design, production and sales teams work as separate entities, each with their own tools, data and objectives, decision-making is slower and inefficiencies are greater. A feasibility concern discovered in production could have been identified at the development stage. Consumer insights gathered during the marketing phase are not passed on to creative teams. These disconnects can result in missed sales opportunities, excess inventory and frustrated customers. ​.

In a recent development, cross-functional collaboration supported by shared data contributes to greater resilience, innovation and growth. Research indicates that cross-functional, team-focused transformations can drive a 30% increase in efficiency. When information flows freely across an interconnected value chain, decisions happen faster, errors are identified earlier and fewer resources are wasted.

Sources indicate that one of the most tangible benefits of data-based collaboration is its impact on time to market, which remains a critical challenge for global fashion brands. While some fashion players can develop and launch products in a matter of days, others still operate on timelines of six to nine months. Closing this gap requires rethinking product development from the earliest creative stages and ensuring continuity of information across the entire product life cycle.

Beyond improving collaboration, these solutions help preserve and scale expertise by making institutional knowledge, technical know-how and historical product data accessible across the organization. Along with accelerating onboarding and decision-making, this helps brands ensure that valuable expertise is retained and leveraged across generations of teams.

Recent findings suggest that data-based collaboration requires a shared infrastructure capable of integrating multiple functions and partners. Solutions embedded with AI and digitalization are the key enablers of this transformation. While product life cycle management (PLM) solutions remain essential for product data management, governance and life cycle visibility, a fresh generation of AI-enabled product development solutions is emerging to support the day-to-day workflow of bringing a product from concept to production.

Sources indicate that by bringing together internal teams, as well as a brand’s global network of suppliers, subcontractors and partners, these solutions ensure that all stakeholders are aligned and working from the same up-to-date information. Companies can capture and communicate data on designs, tech packs, materials, costs, timelines and suppliers in a common framework that cross-functional teams can rely on as products progress.

When each team member has a 360-degree vision of the product in its journey, there are fewer surprises and improved coordination.

The case for shared data infrastructure becomes even more urgent in light of upcoming traceability and sustainability regulations. The Digital Product Passport (DPP), part of the European Union’s Ecodesign for Sustainable Products Regulation, will require products sold in the EU in 2027 to carry structured, standardized product information. Even in the early phase of implementation, which will be a minimal, simplified version of the digital product passport, companies will be expected to provide data on material composition, origin, carbon footprint, supply chain traceability, recyclability, care, durability and chemical compliance.

Compliance will require alignment across the full product cycle. While the first phase will most likely only require supply chain traceability up to Tier 1 and Tier 2 suppliers, adopting a digital traceability approach that starts with the original fibers that will eventually be used in garments and other products provides the foundation for visibility across all tiers of the supply chain. Artificial intelligence is a key enabler of this tracing technology. It continuously monitors transactions to detect inconsistencies or fraudulent claims, enabling brands to move from theoretical commitments to proven actions. Companies that build this infrastructure now will be positioned to leverage transparency as a competitive advantage.

Recent findings suggest that collaborative solutions are reshaping how work is organized, executed and experienced. Beyond enabling basic communication, they support latest ways of working that emphasize shared visibility and consistency across teams. In a business environment increasingly characterized by volatility, complexity and rapid change, these platforms are becoming an key enabler for companies seeking to operate more efficiently and rapidly.

By Geoffrey Seiler – Nov 25, 2026 at 6:04PM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Space Exploration Technologies ›.

The odds of Space Exploration Technologies (SPCX +1.30%) and Tesla (TSLA -1.18%) merging sometime next year have been growing. Prediction market odds jumped earlier this month after Elon Musk's biographer, Walter Isaacson, told CNBC he was confident a merger is coming, since keeping the companies separate makes no sense. This was followed by the two companies picking board members to begin official merger talks.

According to recent reports, isaacson's comments raised the odds that SpaceX would announce a merger with Tesla before March 1, 2027, from 27% on Nov. 11, 2026, to 62% two days later. They now sit at 67%, as of Nov. 24 on Kalshi. Meanwhile, the odds of a merger announcement before the end of 2027 are at 89% on Polymarket.

Now, a merger isn't a foregone conclusion and does face some hurdles, but it does seem very likely at this point. The Democrats' sweeping victories in the midterm elections complicate matters a bit, as Texas Attorney General-elect Nathan Johnson told Bloomberg that a potential merger would face "tremendous scrutiny." Meanwhile, more than half of all Tesla shareholders would need to vote to approve the merger, not just those who decide to vote. Musk owns nearly 20% of the company, but Tesla also has a significant retail shareholder base that would have to vote on the deal for it to pass.

Despite these obstacles, there is still a very good shot that the companies announce a merger next year and complete it by the end of 2028. In such a scenario, it would be best to purchase shares of Tesla, the acquired company. With a little over $5,000, an investor could buy around 13 shares of Tesla.

An acquisition of Tesla by SpaceX ultimately makes a lot of sense. First, it unites Musk's two largest companies and will allow him to focus on a single vision instead of splitting his time between the two. Second, the companies already have an crucial joint venture in the form of their massive chip manufacturing facility, Terafab, so it would make sense to have this under one roof. Finally, the companies' businesses complement each other.

More than anything, both SpaceX and Tesla are about the future, and together they give Musk and investors more shots on goal. Meanwhile, SpaceX could ultimately need some of Tesla's technology to build its planned data centers in space, including solar and Optimus robots. As such, the deal makes sense from a synergy perspective, and the company would be able to cut some overlapping corporate costs.

According to recent reports, any merger between SpaceX and Tesla is likely to be an all-stock deal in which Tesla is acquired at a premium. Analysts at HSBC recently pegged the most likely premium around 33% based on past similar deals, which makes sense.

Based on that premium and current prices, investors would get a little over 4 SpaceX shares for each Tesla share they hold. That would turn investors' 13 Tesla shares into 52 SpaceX shares after the merger, worth $5,000.

Recent findings suggest that for a combined SpaceX-Tesla, the stock would likely trade based on a forward price-to-sales (P/S) ratio. For 2029, the Tesla revenue consensus estimate is $146 billion, while SpaceX's is roughly $336 billion. Combined, that's $482 billion in estimated annual revenue for 2029.

Place a 12-times multiple on that, given its strong growth outlook, and the combined organization would be worth $5.8 trillion. Meanwhile, following the merger, it would have roughly 29.7 billion shares. That would value SpaceX at approximately $195. Those 52 shares would then be worth about $10,150, approximately double a $5,000 initial investment in two years.

This makes Tesla a top growth stock to buy ahead of a potential SpaceX merger.

Industry observers note that have I considered giving water-filtering straws as stocking stuffers this year? Maybe.

But what about your money? If your area was hit by a natural disaster or your bank had an outage, are your finances ready?

According to recent reports, dan Stanush, senior financial planner at Charles Schwab in Asheville, North Carolina, recalls how fast financial conveniences disappeared after Hurricane Helene hit in 2024. “We lost power for three weeks and water for six weeks,” he noted in an email. “And some local businesses could only accept cash or checks because card systems and ATMs were down.”.

It has been revealed that don’t get caught unprepared. Here are the moves experts suggest to help you weather various types of emergencies:.

Recent findings suggest that last week’s Chase outage was a good reminder that access to your bank balance can be disrupted. Stash at least enough cash at home — in small bills — to cover one week of expenses, says Jeff Judge, a certified financial planner (CFP) with Chesapeake Financial Planners in Forest Hill, Maryland.

In a recent development, if systems go down, ATMs can go down with them, said Eileen Olson, a CFP with Emerald Wealth in Daufuskie Island, South Carolina, in an email. Keeping cash in a safe at home is a good blueprint, but it’s also smart to carry cash when you travel. (Remember when planes were grounded nationwide a week and a half ago?).

“My parents and sister were traveling overseas on 9/11 and got stuck much longer than they expected,” Olson remarked. “After that, they always traveled with more cash.”.

In a recent development, if your primary bank and its app were down, would you be able to pay bills? Having an account at more than one bank gives you an alternate funding source. Consider opening a high-yield savings account at a second bank or credit union for your emergency fund.

According to recent reports, “This is the step I push hardest,” Judge notes. “I had a client whose debit card, credit card and savings all ran through one bank, so when that bank’s system went down, she couldn’t even buy gas.”.

According to recent reports, if you don’t want to open a second bank account, a second credit card from a different bank and preferably on a different network (i.e. Visa vs. Mastercard) can provide another way to pay for things. “If there’s a problem with one credit card network, I have a backup with two other credit cards,” states Tony Steuer, author of “Get Ready! A Step-by-Step Planner for Maintaining Your Financial First Aid Kit.”.

In a recent development, make a printed list of your accounts, along with account numbers and key contact numbers. Include your bank, insurers, credit card companies and any financial professionals. Store the list with copies of essential paperwork, including insurance policies and their declarations pages, estate planning documents, legal certificates and identification — potentially in a fire-resistant file box.

Keep a digital copy of your documents in a password-protected, encrypted spot as well. A password manager can store all of your login info.

Joon Um, a CFP with Secure Tax & Accounting in Beverly Hills, California, suggests digital storage site Everplans to his clients, but there are a variety of sites that offer encrypted document storage.

It has been revealed that take some time to write down how you’d pay for groceries, gas and medication if your usual payment methods weren’t available. What expenses would you need to cover first? What recurring bills are on autopay? Where would you keep the cash and any key documents you’d want to take with you if you had to leave home? Make sure other household members know where everything is.

According to recent reports, and set a reminder to update your records at regular intervals. Steuer, for instance, saves his account statements as PDFs and prints everything out once a year. “One of the significant concerns is that people could conceivably break into your 401(k) and drain your 401(k) account,” he notes. Account statements could help if a hack affects any financial balances.

It all adds up to a web of protection that (hopefully) you’ll never have to use.

“The goal is not to anticipate every scenario,” mentioned Schwab's Dan Stanush, “but to have enough flexibility to meet basic needs while systems come back online.”.

#119616. Industry News: When Days Matter: Navigating The AI-Accelerated Exploit Lifecycle

📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1044 w)
📖 Baca
AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Forbes ↗ Open Full Page

Industry News: When Days Matter: Navigating The AI-Accelerated Exploit Lifecycle

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1044 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Forbes

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Eoin Keary Founder & CEO of Edgescan, an enterprise CTEM (Continuous Testing and Exposure Management platform) used by Fortune 500s.
  • Sources indicate that ​AI is fundamentally changing the velocity of the threat landscape, particularly the time between vulnerability discovery and weaponization.
  • This creates a newly introduced imperative: Security processes designed around periodic assessment and remediation must evolve to operate at the speed of continuous change.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Eoin Keary Founder & CEO of Edgescan, an enterprise CTEM (Continuous Testing and Exposure Management platform) used by Fortune 500s.

Sources indicate that ​AI is fundamentally changing the velocity of the threat landscape, particularly the time between vulnerability discovery and weaponization. Vulnerabilities that historically took months, or even up to a year, to become active exploits can now move into the wild within days. AI also expands the attack surface itself as organizations deploy AI systems and agents across their environments, including systems that may not be fully visible to security teams.​.

This creates a newly introduced imperative: Security processes designed around periodic assessment and remediation must evolve to operate at the speed of continuous change. They should consider a different approach to security that employs AI to manage data volume while retaining a human in the loop for critical decision making. In this way, their organizations can rise with the tide of AI-driven threats by purifying their cybersecurity data to ensure it remains manageable and actionable.​.

It has been revealed that the fundamental challenge in vulnerability management has never been finding vulnerabilities but determining which findings represent genuine, actionable risk. Organizations must distinguish between false positives, vulnerabilities that are real but not exploitable and vulnerabilities that are exploitable but mitigated by other controls.​.

Only after those layers of validation can security teams determine which remaining vulnerabilities represent the greatest business risk and should be addressed first. AI threatens to amplify the existing “vulnerability noise” problem by dramatically increasing the volume of findings entering the security team’s workflow. The answer can’t be asking already-constrained security and development teams to manually process an increasingly powerful “firehose” of alerts.​.

In a recent development, slowing down detection isn’t the answer. A better answer is to add a validation layer between detection and action. The value of continuous assessment is its ability to provide a more current view of the environment. Without validation, however, it just produces more noise, faster. This is especially notable as AI accelerates both vulnerability discovery and vulnerability exploitation.

The temptation to use AI to automate remediation and allow systems to patch vulnerabilities without human intervention is obvious.​ Yet autonomous remediation can introduce significant operational risk when an AI system lacks the business context necessary to understand the consequences of its actions. AI should be used to make security professionals “more bionic,” processing information, accelerating analysis and supporting decisions, while humans retain responsibility for critical remediation decisions.​.

As for technical vulnerability data, it alone is insufficient to determine what an organization should fix first. Effective prioritization requires context about the affected asset, its criticality, its role in the business, its data flows and the potential consequences of exploitation. AI can help organizations apply and process this context at scale, but only if the underlying security data is accurate, validated and meaningful.

For teams already buried in findings, the promise of less noise is appealing. The questions start when we discuss what adopting it involves. How much of their time will we need? Will it work with their existing tools? Will the findings arriving on their desks actually be any better?

Industry observers note that in conversations with customers and prospective clients, these are always understandable concerns. They’ve heard plenty of promises about making security simpler. They want to know how much work it’ll take to get started and how much work it’ll save them afterwards. Sending over a mountain of alerts and wishing the team good luck is a fairly generous interpretation of helping.

Providers need to be clear about who does the work. If we offer validated findings, the validation is our responsibility. It’s important to establish which findings are real and investigate exploitability and assess relevant controls before passing the results to the customer.

Recent findings suggest that trust is another hurdle. Fewer findings can sound suspicious when the industry has spent years presenting bigger numbers as evidence of a better job. Customers need to see why something has been ruled out or deprioritized, what testing supports that decision and what remains uncertain.

“AI remarked so” isn’t an explanation I’d fancy taking into a board meeting. Show the evidence and let people challenge the conclusion.​.

Privacy and operational security deserve direct answers. What data will the provider access, and where will it be processed? What testing is permitted, and who approved it? Clear boundaries, documented data handling and named responsibilities help customers assess this service properly. They shouldn’t need a detective to work out what they’re signing up for.

Sources indicate that yes, cost always comes up, but the subscription is only part of the calculation. Investigating false positives, chasing findings that can’t be reproduced and passing inconclusive tickets between teams all costs money. Those hours don’t become free because they’re missing from the procurement spreadsheet. Providers must demonstrate the reduction in effort for the client and explain the price they charge.

The practical route is to start with a defined scope and agree what success looks like with security development and the budget owner. Measure the time spent investigating findings, the quality of evidence reaching developers and how rapidly confirmed risks receive attention. Make implementation manageable, work with existing systems and show the results. That gives each team a reason to support adoption.​​.

According to recent reports, organizations need greater visibility into their attack surface and a continuous understanding of what they’re trying to secure. Continuous assessment and visibility will become increasingly important as the pace of vulnerability discovery and exploitation accelerates. However, continuous assessment inevitably creates more data, making validation and suppression of irrelevant or low-value findings increasingly important.

Organizations should prioritize security approaches that continuously assess the environment while filtering, validating and contextualizing findings before they reach security and development teams. The ultimate objective isn’t to automate every security decision but to ensure that even as the volume of cybersecurity data grows exponentially, organizations can reduce that information to a manageable number of accurate, contextual and actionable risks.​.

In an AI-accelerated threat landscape, the organizations best positioned to respond will be those that can rise with the tide by purifying their cybersecurity data rather than drowning in it.​​.

10 stocks we like better than Coca-Cola ›.

Coca-Cola (KO -0.03%) has been a great stock to own in 2026.

Shares of the giant beverage maker are up more than 40% year to date (compared with the S&P 500 (^GSPC -0.25%), which has risen just about 4.5% this year).

In addition to that impressive gain, Coca-Cola is also a Dividend King, a tech giant that has raised its dividend for at least 50 consecutive years. In fact, Coke has raised its dividend for 64 consecutive years.

That annual dividend currently stands at $2.12 per share, or $0.53 each quarter.

So, to earn a healthy $1,300 per quarter in dividends, how many shares would you need to own? Well, it's as simple as dividing $1,300 by 0.53.

You would need to own 2,453 shares to generate that much quarterly dividend income. That's a hefty investment: That many shares would cost $240,394 at the current share price of $98.

All that mentioned, I believe Coca-Cola is a very good investment right now for two main reasons. First, the stock has historically held up well in recessions and bear markets. And second, while the rise of GLP-1 drugs is hurting some snack food and beverage companies, about 68% of Coca-Cola's portfolio consists of low- or no-calorie drink options.

So, you might not be able to afford enough KO shares to generate over $1,000 in income per quarter, but an investment in this stock is, in my opinion, a wise one.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Newcastle’s pre-season friendly against Bayer Leverkusen at St James’ Park took a bizarre turn when a kit clash prompted the hosts to change shirts midway through the first half.

The German team’s white away kit with blue trim proved hard to distinguish from Newcastle’s home strip, which has a white back and blue stripes across the shoulders.

During the first-half hydration break, Newcastle decided to change into their lilac third kit, which improved the viewing experience for fans who took to social media to question the original choice of kits.

Newcastle would go on to lose the game 2-1 in fresh manager Matthias Jaissle’s first game at St James’, a result which followed a 3-1 reverse against Everton on Wednesday evening.

Leverkusen, the 2023-24 Bundesliga champions now managed by Spaniard Carles Martínez Novell, scored after just 44 seconds through a powerful Ibrahim Maza strike.

Jaissle’s team found their feet as the first 45 minutes progressed, with Yoane Wissa their biggest attacking threat. The striker endured a difficult first season at the club, but his performances at the World Cup with DR Congo appear to have restored confidence.

Newcastle were level just before half-time, when Malick Thiaw rose highest to plant home a back-post header from a corner. Former Brentford goalkeeper Mark Flekken appealed in vain for a foul, but there was no infringement.

After changing all 10 outfield players at half-time against Everton, Jaissle was more circumspect with second-half substitutes; Rory Finneran for Lewis Miley was the only change before the 80th minute.

In a recent development, newcastle faded though, and the game was won by Victor Boniface scoring just a few minutes after coming on as a substitute. The Nigeria striker wrong-footed Sean Steur with an impudent piece of skill before rolling the ball into the bottom corner.

The North-East club are coming to terms with the departures of Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimarães this summer, as well as manager Eddie Howe. They have one more pre-season friendly to play, against Strasbourg on Sunday, before they begin their Premier League campaign at home to Liverpool.

Newcastle United (4-2-3-1) Hornicek; M Miley (Pivas 81), Thiaw, Botman, Hall; Steur, L Miley (Finneran h-t); Elanga, Woltemade (Neave 86), Barnes; Wissa. Subs Charlton, Harris (g), Sanusi, Johnson.

Bayer Leverkusen (4-2-3-1) Flekken; Vazquez (Tape h-t), Bade, Tapsoba, Gutierrez (Belocian 70); Garcia, Fernandez (Terrier 70); Maza (Boniface 80), Tillman (Doganay 70), Moreira (Tella 80); Kofane (Schick h-t). Subs Hofmann, Arthur, Oermann, Poku, Blaswich (g), Alfa-Ruprecht, Hawighorst, Lomb (g).

Recent findings suggest that referee Michael Oliver (Durham). Attendance 39,059.

A second pre-season defeat in a week for Newcastle. Just like against Everton, they faded in the second 45 minutes but Jaissle decided to leave some tired legs out there for fitness purposes. The performances of Barnes and Wissa were promising, but Newcaslte are giving up chances.

Newcastle had a free-kick with the last kick of the game, but Harvey Barnes loops the delivery straight into Flekken’s gloves.

Schik with a chance to wrap up the victory, but Hornicek saves before Thiaw clears to deny Terrier a tap in on the rebounds.

There will be just three minutes of added time to play.

Elanga fouled near the touchline, but time is running out. The free-kick won by Neave came to nothing.

Chance for Barnes! Good combination play involving Elanga and Wissa down the right, and the ball flashed across the six-yard box. Barnes almost steered it in, but did not make firm enough contact.

Newcastle attacking with more urgency since conceding, but there are moans and groans in the ground at a misplaced Elanga pass. Sean Neave has just replaced Woltemade, and the 19-year-old wins a free-kick in a crossing position with his first action of the game.

The striker has only been on the pitch a few minutes, but Boniface has restored Leverkusen’s lead. Lovely chop inside the box, which sent Steur for a hot dog, before passing the ball into the far corner. No celebration of note from a player who could be on the move this summer.

Newcastle making just their second change of the game: Pivas replaces Mason Miley at right-back.

Leverkusen have made two more changes: Moreira and Maza off, Tella and Boniface on.

The corner is straight down the throat of Flekken, and that prompsts some groans from the home fans.

Sources indicate that newcastle having to defend deep for long periods, but Elanga did well to win a free-kick with little support. Moreira dragged the winger down. Then Wissa’s cross is turned behind for a corner.

Woltemade’s control lets him down as he tries to bring the ball down on halfway. The game is being played at a snail’s pace at the moment, but Leverkusen are dominating the ball.

In a recent development, play has now resumed. Garcia does well to defend after Lewis Hall won the ball back in a dangerous position.

Time for another hydration break and Leverkusen are making three more substitutions. We await further changes from Jaissle. Should the game finish level, there will be a penalty shoot-out to decide the winner of the Visit Malta Cup.

Rather like the mid-week friendly against Everton, Newcastle have faded after half-time. Struggling to get into the game in any meaningful way. Slick football from Leverkusen but Fernandez fails to bring the ball under his spell in the box when there was time and space to shoot.

Leverkusen just inches away from regaining the lead. It was an incisive run off the left from Afonso Moreira, who tried to place the ball into the far corner but his attempt rolled just wide of the post.

Good defensive header by Lewis Hall before Wissa wins a foul on halfway. Newcastle feeding off scraps at the moment. Elanga goes too early and is flagged offside.

Sources indicate that bayer Leverkusen have had the better of it in this half, but some of the shooting has been wayward. This time is it Schik’s turn to slash a shot over the bar. Fouls committed by Finneran and Botman.

It has been revealed that newcastle with a three-on-three on the break after Wissa does well to win the ball back on halfway, but Woltemade was too slow to get his shot away at the end of the move. More good play from Wissa.

Half a chance for Fernandez to shoot from the edge of the D, but he was leaning back and ballooned the shot miles over the bar.

Finneran, the youngster in Newcastle’s midfield, is caught on the ball but then does well to recover it. I reckon there will be a raft of changes on the hour mark.

It has been revealed that corner for Leverkusen after Moreira gets forward and attacks Mason Miley. The German side have additional aerial threat with Schik on the pitch. Woltemade does well to head clear.

Bayer Leverkuen kick off in the second half.

Jaissle made 10 against Everton, so wants his starters to build minutes today. Rory Finneran is coming on for Newcastle, an 18-year-old academy player. He replaces Lewis Miley in midfield. Czech striker Patrik Schik is on for Bayer Leverkusen.

The scoreline is a fair reflection of an even first half, with Wissa Newcastle’s best player. The story though, is that kit clash that prompted Newcastle to change into their lilac third kit halfway through the half.

Just the two minutes of stoppage time to play.

Newcastle equalise from a set-piece. Flekken is claiming a foul, but it is a legitimate goal. The goalkeeper was nowhere to be seen on a corner that looped all the way to be back post, and he seemed to lose his bearings allowing Thiaw to find the far corner.

Newcastle have a corner after another move in which Wissa was lively. His performances have been a ray of light in pre-season, he really struggled in his first season at the club.

Lewis Hall takes the free-kick, but he scoops it well over the bar. Elanga delivers a low cross from the right, but Garcia is well positioned to clear.

Newcastle enjoying a lot more possession now, but you cannot say they look like equalising.

That was better though, more zip in the attack with Elanga laying the ball off for Wissa and Fernandez is booked from dragging the Newcastle forward to the ground. Free-kick in a shooting position.

According to recent reports, good play from Lewis Hall, skipping beyond two challenges to escape from a tight spot but then his crossfield pass is intercepted. Moreira passes the ball straight out of play for a Newcastle goal kick, when there was a chance for Leverkusen to punish the hosts on the break.

It has been revealed that elanga tries to take on Gutierrez but his low cross is too close to Flekken. Gutierrez then buys a foul when under pressure from Lewis Miley. Game has become quite bitty following those stoppages. Maza then chops down Harvery Barnes.

The game is back under way. Changing kits has improved things visually but it is still not ideal. You wonder how on earth two clubs of this stature failed to liaise on this before the game.

Bayer Leverkusen are still on top, but play has been stopped for a hydration break. Some boos from the stands, it is not an especially hot day.

On the subject of the kit clash, Newcastle are now changing into their lilac away kit. Shades of Manchester United at the Dell all those years ago.

A short stoppage in play after Tapsoba receives a knock in the small of the back from Newcastle’s goalkeeper Hornicek. Both managers get their players over for a tactical conflab.

Recent findings suggest that leverkusen look very accomplished in possession, they are moving the ball well through the lines. Kofane was a significant threat when they played Arsenal in last season’s Champions League and they are looking to find him with crosses. Mason Miley defends well at right-back, but at the expense of a corner.

Sources indicate that flekken called into action again, Newcastle starting to warm to their task. It was direct play from first Elanga and then Barnes, but his cross deflects towards the goalkeeper and he parries away. Then Barnes is fouled, and Newcastle have a free-kick in a crossing position near the left corner of the penalty area. Poor delivery from Barnes, Flekken claims.

Newcastle fans sing “walking in a Keegan wonderland” in unison. Bade is then penalised for catching Woltemade late as they contested an aerial challenge.

Recent findings suggest that newcastle’s best moment so far: Wissa peels off the shoulder of Bade and tested Flekken with a volley from a tight angle. The goalkeeper saved and Leverkusen scramble clear, but it was good movement from the Newcastle striker.

Sources indicate that leverkusen continue to make the running, enjoying more possession and most of it is coming inside Newcastle’s half. Goalkeeper Flekken takes a beat inside his own six-yard box, and his pass out is almost cut out by Woltemade.

Newcastle’s players are wearing black armbands in memory of Kevin Keegan.

There is a slightly awkward clash of kits on display: both shirts feature a lot of white, and the blue trim around the shoulders of Newcastle’s home kit is quite similar to Leverkusen’s away strip.

Kofane, who impressed up front last season in Germany, throws himself at a cross.

Industry observers note that fans were barely settled in their seats when Maza’s vicious left-footed strike from outside of the area flew past Hornicek. Cracking goal, not much the goalkeeper could do about it.

Newcastle get the game under way.

According to recent reports, matthias Jaissle walks to the home dugout for the first time as manager. Just eight days until the proper stuff begins against Liverpool, a fixture which tends to throw up entertaining games. Bayer Leverkusen keep the home players waiting in the tunnel.

Recent findings suggest that the former Liverpool defender has been linked with a move to Arsenal this week. Quansah is with his team-mates but not part of the matchday squad.

Bayer Leverkusen XI: Flekken; Gutierrez, Bade, Fernandez, Moreira, Tillman, Tapsoba, Arthur, Garcia, Maza, Kofane.

Subs: Blaswich, Lomb, Hofmann, Terrier, Schick, Oermann, Tape, Poku, Vazquez, Boniface, Tella, Alfa-Ruprecht, Doganay, Hawighorst.

Newcastle XI: Hornicek; M Miley, Thiaw (c), Botman, Hall; Steur, L Miley; Elanga, Woltemade, Barnes; Wissa.

Subs: Harris, Charlton, Pivas, Sanusi, Johnson, Finneran, Neave.

Today's team to take on Bayer Leverkusen in the @VisitMalta Weekender 👊 pic.twitter.com/ZfRvucBXSq.

Newcastle United continue their preparations for the new season with a home friendly against Bayer Leverkusen, hoping to improve on their pretty limp showing against Everton at Murrayfield.

Recent findings suggest that latest manager ​Matthias Jaissle is ‌refusing to dwell on the departure of key players that has left his club in turmoil going into the Premier League season, insisting that he sees opportunity in the situation. Jaissle was recruited from Saudi Pro League side Al-Ahli after Eddie Howe left last month, with the German coach joining a club who had lost Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and captain Bruno Guimaraes in quick succession.

Sources indicate that “It’s a challenge, a massive challenge, always when there’s a transitional period. ‌But it’s ‌not time to ⁠complain, it doesn’t make sense to see the negative things,” Jaissle said.

“We want to see the chance in that situation and that’s our approach from day one. We are here to do our ⁠best job. We want to support the players, the current squad.

In a recent development, “There will be adjustments to see in the coming days, weeks. But for now it’s only focused on the daily work, the work we can influence. That’s all that ​matters now.”.

The 38-year-old coach arrived in Newcastle ‌having won two Austrian Bundesliga titles with Red Bull Salzburg before leading Al-Ahli to back-to-back AFC Champions League crowns.

He remained tight-lipped about newly introduced signings.

“Obviously, in that transition phase, the players who left the club were ‌great ​players, great characters, experienced ⁠players. This is now a vacuum,” he remarked.

Sources indicate that “Either we adjust something in the squad, by signing these players, these profiles, or other players ⁠need to step up and fill ​these positions, these leadership roles. I’m quite optimistic, we can work in both scenarios.”.

Jaissle noted he had a ​clear vision of how he wants his team to play.

“The phrase how Newcastle ‌should play like is front-footed, intense, ​aggressive and of course also successful. ​In the end, it’s all about what ⁠I can ⁠say and it’s also why I’m sitting here,” he mentioned.

“The approach we have as a coaching team and the identity of Newcastle is famed for, it’s so linked so close together - which is a perfect fit in my eyes and ​that’s going to be exciting.”.

    By Eric Volkman – Nov 25, 2026 at 7:10PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than CleanSpark ›.

    According to recent reports, cleanSpark's (CLSK +1.27%) final earnings release of its current fiscal year was published after market hours on Tuesday. The following day, investors indicated their somewhat cautious appreciation for the organization's performance by trading its shares up by almost 1.3%. While not every metric in CleanSpark's fourth quarter was impressive, the company improved several crucial line items.

    We can't say that for net revenue, as it declined to $120.9 million from $223.7 million in the fourth quarter of 2025. That wasn't a shock or surprise, however, as the company's legacy business of Bitcoin (BTC +2.95%) mining was affected by a drop in the crypto's average price while it was building out its artificial intelligence (AI) data center business.

    According to recent reports, the dynamic was much different on the bottom line, where CleanSpark flipped to a net profit of $9.8 million ($0.04 per share) from the year-ago loss of $925,000. Much of this, however, was tied to its legacy business -- it booked a nearly $306 million accounting gain on the value of its Bitcoin, despite the digital currency's recent softening.

    This meant a mixed quarter for CleanSpark, as it whiffed on the analyst consensus estimate of $134.3 million. Yet it trounced the average pundit expectation of a $0.33 per share net loss.

    The firm's results are choppy due to the nature of the Bitcoin mining business, which, for obvious reasons, depends on the cryptocurrency's price. CleanSpark has now entered a pivotal fiscal year for its transformation, as it expects to begin drawing revenue from high-profile clients for AI data center space.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

    Industry observers note that given that, I'd say that investors were buying into CleanSpark based on that high-potential future rather than the unexpected flip into profitability. I'd be even more cautious than those folks. At the same time, though, AI data center operation is almost certainly a durable and lucrative business; this tech giant isn't the only legacy crypto miner making the transition, and it hasn't yet proven it can soar above such peers.

    Tech Report: Vertex Pharmaceuticals Has Turned $10,000 Into $61,660 Over 10 Years. Here's What Could Come Next

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • By Prosper Junior Bakiny – Nov 25, 2026 at 7:12PM EST.
    • 10 stocks we like better than Vertex Pharmaceuticals ›.
    • Vertex Pharmaceuticals (VRTX +0.04%), a biotech company, has been on an impressive run over the past decade.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Prosper Junior Bakiny – Nov 25, 2026 at 7:12PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Vertex Pharmaceuticals ›.

    Vertex Pharmaceuticals (VRTX +0.04%), a biotech company, has been on an impressive run over the past decade. If you had invested $10,000 in the stock in 2016, you'd have about $61,660 today. By comparison, $10,000 invested in the S&P 500 10 years ago would be worth about $38,663 today (with dividends reinvested) -- that's not bad, but it pales in comparison to the returns you would have had with Vertex. That stated, the past is the past. The key question is whether the drugmaker can deliver similarly impressive returns going forward.

    Vertex has crushed broader equity markets thanks to its dominance in the cystic fibrosis (CF) market. The tech giant has very little competition in this niche, and thanks to several new debuts over the past 10 years that have allowed it to treat increasingly more CF patients, revenue and earnings growth have been strong. Vertex's CF franchise should remain an key growth driver over the next decade. After all, the company's most important medicines won't lose patent exclusivity until the late 2030s.

    Sources indicate that but in the meantime, Vertex should significantly diversify and expand its lineup. The firm's work in kidney diseases looks particularly promising. Vertex Pharmaceuticals could earn approval for one product in its kidney disease portfolio, povetacicept -- a medicine for IgA nephropathy -- by the end of the month. This medicine has peak sales potential of around $4 billion across IgA nephropathy and other potential indications, according to some estimates.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

    Of course, that outcome isn't guaranteed yet, not by a long shot. But the point is that Vertex's kidney disease pipeline, with products like povetacicept and others, including inaxaplin and VX-407, looks promising. The biotech leader could, eventually, generate close to $10 billion in peak sales from these products if all goes well. Another area where Vertex could make progress is pain treatments.

    It has already earned approval for Journavx, a medicine for acute pain and the first oral non-opioid pain signal inhibitor ever. Journavx is in several ongoing clinical trials and could earn key label expansions, while Vertex works on other pain treatments. Further, thanks to a recent acquisition, Vertex Pharmaceuticals has an interesting endocrine diseases portfolio that it believes could reach more than $5 billion in annual sales.

    It has been revealed that we haven't even mentioned other newer releases, including Casgevy, a gene-editing medicine for a pair of rare blood diseases. Vertex's potential across its entire pipeline is massive, and even after probability-adjusting sales projections, since pipeline products aren't guaranteed approval, my view is that the tech giant's prospects look promising. That noted, I wouldn't expect Vertex Pharmaceuticals to repeat its performance since 2016 over the next decade.

    Recent findings suggest that that's a tall order for a larger biotech that faces more competition than it did 10 years ago. Even so, from current levels, Vertex is well positioned to beat the market over the long run, making it a great stock to buy.
