    #119603. Industry News: Broadcom Stock Hasn't Traded This Low Since July 2025. I Think It's a Buy.

    📅 26 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (877 w)
    📖 Baca
    Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Fool ↗ Open Full Page

    Industry News: Broadcom Stock Hasn't Traded This Low Since July 2025. I Think It's a Buy.

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (877 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that broadcom (AVGO -0.07%) stock fell about 5% on Wednesday to under $290 as I write, on a day when chip stocks sold off broadly.
    • It has been revealed that the business is going the other way.
    • In a recent development, at its lowest price in over a year, is Broadcom a buy?
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Daniel Sparks – Nov 25, 2026 at 7:43PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Broadcom ›.

    It has been revealed that broadcom (AVGO -0.07%) stock fell about 5% on Wednesday to under $290 as I write, on a day when chip stocks sold off broadly. The slide took the chipmaker to its lowest point since July 2025, even below the $291.53 close it hit on Nov. 5. Shares are now about 40% under June 2's record close of $481.57.

    It has been revealed that the business is going the other way. Management's September guidance was for 93% year-over-year revenue growth in its fiscal fourth quarter of 2026 (the period that ended Nov. 1, 2026). That would be an even faster rate than the quarter before.

    In a recent development, at its lowest price in over a year, is Broadcom a buy? I think so. Today, investors are paying for very little of Broadcom's artificial intelligence (AI) growth. What gives me pause is how few companies that growth relies on.

    Sources indicate that broadcom's revenue growth has accelerated sharply in the last year. For its fiscal third quarter (the period that ended Aug. 2, 2026), sales climbed 86% year over year to $29.6 billion, up from 22% growth the year before. Most of the gain was from AI chips. AI semiconductor revenue more than tripled from the year before, hitting $16.7 billion, or 56% of the total. Non-GAAP (adjusted) earnings per share jumped 96% to $3.32, and free cash flow grew 95% to $13.7 billion.

    Management expects more. Its forecast calls for fiscal 2027 AI revenue of about $115 billion, twice its expected fiscal 2026 total. And on the September earnings call, CEO Hock Tan mentioned Broadcom has already lined up the supply to get there.

    Industry observers note that if Broadcom's fiscal fourth quarter lands where management guided (revenue of $34.8 billion with an adjusted operating margin of 66%), adjusted earnings would be roughly $3.80 per share by my math. Four quarters at that pace would total about $15 per share.

    It has been revealed that today's price, under $290, is about 19 times these earnings. The S&P 500 (^GSPC -0.25%), for comparison, traded at about 17 times forward earnings in FactSet's Nov. 20 report.

    Put another way, even if Broadcom's profits never grew past that quarter's pace, the stock would cost only slightly more than the market on a price-to-earnings basis. And if AI revenue doubles next year as planned, earnings should climb well past that pace.

    With the earnings per share analysts expect on average for fiscal 2027, the price-to-earnings ratio falls to around 15.

    I suspect that low price-to-earnings ratio has a lot to do with how few buyers drive Broadcom's growth. The organization estimates in its latest quarterly filing that its five largest end customers made up around half of its revenue in the first three quarters of fiscal 2026.

    "[I]n some ways, I'm so glad we have only 6 customers to deal with," Tan said on the September call, talking about the buyers of Broadcom's custom AI chips. He'd just laid out the shortages, from power to memory, that control when a customer's AI data center can come online.

    For shareholders, though, this short list is the main risk. As of Aug. 2, Broadcom had committed to buy around $127 billion in supplies, mainly inventory, and its filing warns that customers might cancel or delay orders over complications like a lack of capital or delayed AI build-outs.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/25/26.

    Broadcom also disclosed in October that it's backstopping part of the financing for one customer's AI racks. Its maximum potential liability is around $43 billion, but it thinks the chances of having to pay are low. If one big customer cuts back, Broadcom might feel it in its sales and in these commitments at the same time.

    Industry observers note that broadcom stock dropped 12% on Nov. 20. That morning, analyst Ming-Chi Kuo of TF International Securities posted that his industry survey found Google, owned by Alphabet, cutting its planned 2027 shipments of one Broadcom-designed line of its custom AI chips by around 20%. Neither tech giant has confirmed that.

    Sources indicate that but Tan noted in September that four of the six customers, Google included, are financially strong enough to fund their build-outs themselves. And in April, Broadcom disclosed a long-term deal to develop and supply Google's future generations of custom AI chips. Tan said Broadcom looks to ship tens of billions of dollars in chips to Google each year for the next several years.

    Because investors are paying so little for next year's growth, I think Broadcom stock is a buy below $290. But with so much of fiscal 2027 riding on six customers, I'd start with a small position and build it up gradually.

    #119599. Breaking: 19 Business Upgrades To Maximize The Value Of Real-Time Payments

    📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1325 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Forbes ↗ Open Full Page

    Breaking: 19 Business Upgrades To Maximize The Value Of Real-Time Payments

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1325 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Forbes

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • As instant-payment networks such as FedNow and the RTP network reach more financial institutions, more businesses have the opportunity to send and receive funds within seconds, even on weekends and holidays.
    • For many companies, the transition to real-time payments will require a fresh look at the internal technology and business practices that support financial operations.
    • Update ERP payment reconciliation and the capacity behind it.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    As instant-payment networks such as FedNow and the RTP network reach more financial institutions, more businesses have the opportunity to send and receive funds within seconds, even on weekends and holidays. However, taking full advantage of that speed requires more than gaining access to a fresh payment network. Legacy workflows built around batch processing and traditional banking hours can create delays and operational gaps even when money moves instantly.

    For many companies, the transition to real-time payments will require a fresh look at the internal technology and business practices that support financial operations. Below, Forbes Technology Council members share ways companies can modernize their systems and processes to make real-time payments more efficient, secure and beneficial to the business.

    Update ERP payment reconciliation and the capacity behind it. From my experience leading fintech integration projects, connecting payment channels is only part of the work. Internal systems must confirm transactions, update balances and flag duplicates at any hour. Adopt API-driven, automated reconciliation with exception handling, and load-test it at peak volume without maintenance windows. - Mohammad Sharif Daoud, Global Center for AI Excellence.

    Sources indicate that combine automated matching with clear ownership of exceptions. Routine transactions should reconcile automatically, while unmatched payments, short payments and missing remittance details are routed to accountable teams for timely resolution. This approach reduces manual effort, improves visibility into available cash, and helps finance teams put incoming funds to work sooner while resolving discrepancies faster. - Venus Garg, Elevance Health.

    In a recent development, forbes Technology Council is an invitation-only community for world-class CIOs, CTOs and technology executives. Do I qualify?

    Recent findings suggest that providers and participants in the expanding instant payments ecosystem must modernize risk assessment alongside payment infrastructure. Instant settlement leaves little room for error, while added verification and manual review undermine speed. Richer financial data and streamlined fraud, liquidity and other risk assessments can enable more instant payments without sacrificing sound controls. - Brian Reshefsky, EDGE.

    Industry observers note that companies should modernize their treasury and cash management systems. Real-time payments mean little if reconciliation, liquidity management and reporting remain outdated. Integrating automation, AI-driven forecasting and real-time financial visibility enables businesses to optimize cash flow, reduce risk and make faster, smarter capital decisions. - Paul Kerslake, N3XUS.

    According to recent reports, payment routing deserves more attention. Many companies choose how to send money based on fixed bank relationships or manual processes. Connecting internal systems to multiple payment networks lets them route each payment based on cost, availability and whether the recipient can receive it instantly. That makes real-time payments useful across the business instead of within a single network. - Maghnus Mareneck, Cosmos Labs.

    Sources indicate that I’d modernize how procurement negotiates supplier payment terms. If a tech giant can pay immediately upon verified delivery, procurement should be able to negotiate something in return, such as a discount, better pricing or priority access to inventory. That requires procurement and finance to agree on when using cash sooner is worthwhile. The opportunity is to make payment speed part of the negotiation. - Kacee Johnson, radical.

    In a recent development, fraud detection and payment authorization need to evolve with real-time payments. When money moves instantly, there’s little time to detect fraud or reverse a transaction. Companies need real-time fraud analysis and stronger verification that a payment was genuinely authorized by the customer, without slowing down legitimate transactions. - Alex Spokoiny, Check Point Software.

    Patch cash and liquidity management. When payments settle around the clock, including weekends, treasury can’t rely on end-of-day positions and cutoff times. Modernize to real-time cash visibility and automated funding of accounts so you can pay and collect any time without tying up idle balances. - Aruna Veerappan, Upwork Global Inc.

    Recent findings suggest that customer-facing billing and refund workflows should be modernized to take full advantage of real-time payments. Many companies still rely on multi-day settlement, batch disbursements and manual refund processes that frustrate customers accustomed to instant transactions. Modernized workflows deliver instant payouts, real-time refunds and transparent payment status, improving customer experience and loyalty. - Nitin Agarwal, Luminace.

    Recent findings suggest that companies should modernize how they track incoming payments. What’s the point of receiving money in seconds if accounting takes two days to recognize it? It’s like getting a package delivered instantly but waiting until tomorrow to open the door. Real-time payments need real-time accounting. - Margarita Simonova, ILoveMyQA.

    Companies should modernize their payment approval workflows to keep pace with instant-payment networks. If a supplier payment still waits until the next business day for approval, the money may move instantly, but the business hasn’t gained much. Setting approval limits and delegating authority in advance lets routine payments go through around the clock, while larger or unusual transactions still get reviewed before funds leave the account. - Elton Chan, Second Talent.

    Modernize the payment decisioning and exception-management architecture. Real-time settlement atop batch-era fraud controls, liquidity monitoring, reconciliation and exception handling merely accelerates operational risk. 24/7 money movement demands 24/7 intelligence, controls and accountability. Speed without trust is a liability. - Rajjie Sarmey, FutureProof CXO™.

    According to recent reports, companies should modernize their liquidity orchestration layer, not just payment gateways. Real-time payments require real-time intelligence across treasury, fraud detection, reconciliation and cash forecasting. The next frontier is agentic liquidity management, where AI continuously anticipates cash needs, dynamically allocates funds and optimizes working capital. Instant settlement should enable instant financial decisions. - Nicola Sfondrini, PWC.

    Sources indicate that real-time payments won’t automatically create value. I’d challenge the premise that modernizing one process or internal system is enough. Companies need to assess technical debt, process debt and data debt together. Money can move instantly while the business operates on yesterday’s information. The question leaders need to focus on is whether the entire organization can access and act on that data. - Neda Nia, Stibo Systems.

    Modernize how you approve and double-check payouts before money goes out the door. Older payment methods gave finance teams until the end of the day to catch a duplicate invoice, a wrong account or a bad refund before the bank processed it. With instant payments, the money is gone in seconds, so your approval rules and mistake checks have to happen up front, before anyone clicks “Send.” - Vatsal Bhardwaj, Jabali.ai.

    Industry observers note that update collections and customer communication. If payment status reaches the CRM overnight, customers who paid at 9 a.m. still get an overdue reminder at noon. At one client, about one in 10 dunning emails went to accounts that had already paid. Streaming payment events into Salesforce stopped those messages, cut “I already paid” support cases by roughly 35%, and released credit holds the same day. - Sergii Grushai, Peeklogic.

    Industry observers note that modernize tax determination and allocation. When a customer pays instantly, the tech giant should reserve sales tax, VAT and withholding by jurisdiction and legal entity. Many firms calculate these obligations later from batch reports, overstating available cash and rushing remittances. Link payment events to tax rules and entity records, then test reversals and partial payments so speed does not create a compliance backlog. This clearly separates cash from tax owed. - Jagadish Gokavarapu, Wissen Infotech.

    Your customer service layer needs modernization. Here’s why: Real-time payments are final. There’s no recall window. So the “Here’s my money, can I cancel it?” questions spike, and they need answers in seconds, not tomorrow. In our banking data, payments and money movement drive roughly 36% of guided-task volume. Instant money needs instant, accurate answers. - Merlin Bise, Inbenta.

    Recent findings suggest that companies should integrate instant-payment networks directly with their ERP or through treasury platforms, ensuring cash inflows and outflows are reflected in real time. Payment initiation, status updates, and automated AR and AP matching can enable straight-through processing, reduce manual intervention and improve cash visibility. This aligns financial operations with payment speed, improving efficiency and working capital management. - Eranda Maldeniya, Enterprise Analytics.

    Porter, 26, underwent knee surgery in April and was waived by the Bucks just days before the first game of the regular season.

    Porter — whose 2025-26 season was delayed due to a knee injury — was out to a great start with the Bucks last season, averaging 17.4 points and 7.4 assists. But he was limited to just 38 games after sustaining another knee injury, this one forcing him to undergo surgery in April.

    Recent findings suggest that despite proving he was healthy, Porter remained on the free-agent market for over a month before reportedly joining the Magic. He also met with the Denver Nuggets during the season.

    Once he signs, Porter will join his fifth NBA team since being drafted in the first round of the 2019 NBA Draft.

    Porter has had some off-the-court complications that have contributed to his vagabond NBA journey, most notably pleading guilty to misdemeanor assault and a harassment violation in Newly introduced York in 2024 in a case involving former girlfriend and ex-WNBA player Kysre Gondrezick.
